item.title: Singapore's Zerra DC lands Macquarie backing for Asia-Pacific data center expansion
item.description: Singapore-based data center developer Zerra DC has secured an investment from Macquarie Capital to expand its hyperscale platform across Asia-Pacific, the company said on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Singapore-based data center developer Zerra DC has secured an investment from Macquarie Capital to expand its hyperscale platform across Asia-Pacific, the company said on Tuesday. Here are some more details: Financial terms of the investment were not disclosed. The investment builds on Macquarie Capital’s existing relationship with Zerra at Western Downs Digital Park (WDDP) in Queensland. Zerra said it will develop and operate the WDDP campus, with Macquarie Capital participating as a consortium partner and project and financial adviser. The firm's current development pipeline comprises more than 2 gigawatts of planned IT capacity across Australia, Japan and India. Investments in Asia-Pacific data center buildouts have been gathering pace, with Australian data center operator [USN:L1N41D03I TEXT:"AirTrunk committing $3 billion in April"] to build two hyperscale data centers in Malaysia. Zerra added Grant Samuel acted as financial adviser for the deal.

item.title: West Virginia commit Chris Wilson Jr. killed in shooting
item.description: West Virginia football commit Chris Wilson Jr., a four-star defensive end prospect from Indiana, was shot and killed early Monday morning in Muncie, Ind. He was 17.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: West Virginia football commit Chris Wilson Jr., a four-star defensive end prospect from Indiana, was shot and killed early Monday morning in Muncie, Ind. He was 17. Muncie police are investigating the shooting after finding Wilson inside a vehicle with multiple gunshot wounds in the 1400 block of East Cromer Avenue. According to police, emergency dispatchers received a report of gunfire at approximately 2:59 a.m. Wilson was pronounced dead at the scene. Authorities have not identified a suspect or released a possible motive. Wilson was a senior at Yorktown High School and one of Indiana's highest-rated football recruits in the Class of 2027. He committed to West Virginia in June, choosing the Mountaineers over offers from Auburn, Cincinnati, Purdue and several other Division I programs. The 235-pound edge rusher was ranked 31st at his position nationally and sixth overall in Indiana, according to the Rivals Industry Rankings. Wilson recorded 25 tackles, including four sacks, and an interception during his junior season in 2025, helping Yorktown capture a Class 4A sectional championship. He had 12 tackles and a sack through five games this season. Yorktown principal Stacey Brewer confirmed Wilson's death Monday in a message to students and families, saying his family had given the school permission to release the information. "With great sadness, I share that Chris Wilson, a senior at Yorktown High School, died tragically early this morning," Brewer wrote. "Chris was a valued member of our school, our football team, and our community. Our hearts are with his family, friends, and teammates." The school also informed families that local authorities had determined there was no ongoing threat to students or school facilities. Counselors will be available when classes resume following the school's fall break. Wilson was among the highest-ranked players in West Virginia's incoming recruiting class and was expected to join the Mountaineers next year. "The West Virginia football program is heartbroken by the news of the tragic loss of Chris Wilson Jr. this morning," coach Rich Rodriguez said Monday in a prepared statement. "We really enjoyed getting to know Chris during the recruiting process. The WVU football program sends its heartfelt thoughts and prayers to Chris' family in this difficult time." Police said the investigation remains ongoing. --Field Level Media

item.title: Operadora da Wikipedia diz que IA da OpenAI pode estar ligada à interrupção de serviços
item.description: A Fundação Wikimedia, que administra a enciclopédia online Wikipédia, afirmou nesta segunda-feira que o tráfego intenso proveniente de agentes de inteligência artificial da OpenAI pode estar relacionado às interrupções que seu serviço de dados sofreu em maio.
item.dc:creator: Raphael Satter
item.content:encoded: A Fundação Wikimedia, que administra a enciclopédia online Wikipédia, afirmou nesta segunda-feira que o tráfego intenso proveniente de agentes de inteligência artificial da OpenAI pode estar relacionado às interrupções que seu serviço de dados sofreu em maio. A Wikimedia afirmou que pode confirmar “que descobrimos algumas atividades desses agentes ‘não autorizados’ da OpenAI nas plataformas da Wikimedia”, incluindo um incidente ocorrido em maio que resultou em uma “interrupção parcial” do serviço de consulta do Wikidata. A entidade afirmou que a interrupção parece ter sido desencadeada quando os agentes de IA da OpenAI acessaram milhões de páginas e realizaram centenas de milhares de consultas de dados. A Wikimedia também afirmou que a IA da OpenAI fez edições não autorizadas nos sites wiki da Wikimedia, incluindo “edições potencialmente maliciosas” em uma ferramenta de citação que, segundo a fundação, provavelmente tinham como objetivo se apropriar dela. A ferramenta de anotações Etherpad também foi afetada por atividades da IA da OpenAI. A OpenAI não respondeu imediatamente a um pedido feito pela Reuters para comentário.

item.title: Mercado financeiro argentino recupera forças com resultado eleitoral no Brasil
item.description: O mercado financeiro argentino operou com alta generalizada nesta segunda-feira após Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) liderar o primeiro turno das eleições presidenciais no Brasil na véspera, fator que ajudou a mobilizar liquidez na região, afirmaram operadores.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O mercado financeiro argentino operou com alta generalizada nesta segunda-feira após Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) liderar o primeiro turno das eleições presidenciais no Brasil na véspera, fator que ajudou a mobilizar liquidez na região, afirmaram operadores. A melhora dos preços foi registrada após quedas significativas no mercado doméstico e foi apoiada por uma demanda por ações do setor financeiro e títulos atrelados ao dólar. O principal índice da bolsa de Buenos Aires, o S&P Merval (.MERV) , fechou com alta de 3,68%, com destaque para o desempenho dos papéis dos bancos BBVA (BBARm.BA) e Macro (BMAm.BA) , com 5,63% e 5,24%, respectivamente. O índice havia caído 4,36% na semana passada. O Brasil é o principal parceiro comercial da Argentina. No domingo, Flávio -- que tem o apoio do presidente argentino Javier Milei -- ficou cerca de 2 pontos percentuais à frente do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), que busca a reeleição, no primeiro turno eleitoral: 47,03% contra 45,16%. “Consideramos que o resultado eleitoral de ontem (domingo) no Brasil é favorável para a Argentina. A vantagem de dois pontos de Bolsonaro o deixa à beira da vitória, e acreditamos que um real mais forte, taxas mais baixas e a presença de um aliado natural dentro do Mercosul favorecem os planos do presidente Milei”, afirmou a consultoria Max Capital. Enquanto isso, o peso argentino interbancário se valorizou muito levemente, em 0,07%, para 1.520,5 unidades por dólar na venda. Os títulos argentinos no mercado de balcão valorizaram 0,9% em média, enquanto o risco-país da Argentina caiu para 615 pontos básicos (17h no horário de Brasília), após atingir 655 pontos na sexta-feira, seu nível mais alto em 10 meses. (Reportagem de Hernán Nessi e Jorge Otaola)

item.title: Escritor e político britânico Jeffrey Archer morre aos 86 anos
item.description: Jeffrey Archer, o romancista britânico best-seller e ex-político que foi preso por mentir em um caso de difamação de grande repercussão, faleceu aos 86 anos, informou sua editora, a HarperCollins, nesta segunda-feira.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Jeffrey Archer, o romancista britânico best-seller e ex-político que foi preso por mentir em um caso de difamação de grande repercussão, faleceu aos 86 anos, informou sua editora, a HarperCollins, nesta segunda-feira. Archer vendeu mais de 300 milhões de exemplares em todo o mundo e era conhecido por thrillers cheios de ritmo. Entre os livros publicados em português estão "Cara ou Coroa" e "Eis aqui um homem". Seu último romance, “Adam and Eve”, deve ser publicado ainda este mês. Ele também foi um proeminente político conservador, que atuou brevemente como parlamentar antes de se tornar um alto dirigente do partido sob o governo da primeira-ministra Margaret Thatcher, em meados da década de 1980. Mas Archer sofreu uma queda muito pública quando foi condenado por perjúrio e obstrução da justiça em 2001, recebendo uma sentença de quatro anos de prisão. Kate Elton, presidente-executiva da HarperCollins no Reino Unido e editora de Archer, disse em um comunicado: “Estamos todos devastados por termos perdido um escritor que trouxe alegria a gerações de leitores — e um verdadeiro amigo.”

item.title: Next Artemis mission on track for 2027, but anything can happen, astronaut says
item.description: The next mission under NASA's Artemis moon program could still launch next summer as planned, but "anything can happen" given the remaining development work for the two lunar landers needed for the mission, one of the Artemis III astronauts told Reuters.
item.dc:creator: Joey Roulette
item.content:encoded: The next mission under NASA's Artemis moon program could still launch next summer as planned, but "anything can happen" given the remaining development work for the two lunar landers needed for the mission, one of the Artemis III astronauts told Reuters. NASA's third Artemis mission will be the first to involve the program's moon landers — SpaceX's (SPCX.O) Starship and Blue Origin's Blue Moon. Unlike [USN:L1N40O056 TEXT:"Artemis II"], the spacecraft will stay in Earth's orbit to perform crewed docking demonstrations with Orion, a capsule whose job is to transfer the astronaut crew to the landers after getting them into space. "The biggest thing is having faith in the team to pull together, with the same rationale that anything can happen," Artemis III mission specialist Andre Douglas said in an interview on Monday, when asked if Artemis III is still on track for launch next year. Douglas, 40, fellow NASA astronauts Randy Bresnik and Frank Rubio, as well as Italian astronaut Luca Parmitano, were tapped this year as [USN:L1N42H10R TEXT:"the crew for Artemis III"], seen as a key rehearsal before NASA attempts to put astronauts on the lunar surface in 2028 in Artemis IV. Both companies' lunar landers have had [USN:L1N42601G TEXT:"schedule"] [USN:L1N3ZY0WT TEXT:"delays"] while facing an unchecked list of complex development tasks, such as demonstrating the ability to store and delicately transfer super-cooled propellants in space and dock with another object in orbit. "Those are the major ones," Douglas said of the milestones the contractors need to achieve before the mission. While some industry sources doubt the landers will be ready in time for a 2027 mission, NASA has been [USN:L6N43M0HV TEXT:"optimistic"], with administrator Jared Isaacman citing good progress for "the parts that are in NASA's greatest control," referring to the NASA-owned Orion and its Space Launch System rocket. Starship and Blue Moon have received billions of dollars in NASA funding while their development remains privately managed, a commercial-focused contracting model that has given NASA relatively little control over the manner and speed with which the companies build their landers. "We just have to keep putting our heads down, leaning forward, and trying to meet the ideal timeline, which would be June of next year," said Douglas, who works with both SpaceX and Blue Origin on their lander development. He added that he and other NASA officials plan to meet with SpaceX and Blue Origin over the next few months to determine their spacecraft's readiness. The Artemis III mission had originally been planned as the program's first moon landing until February, when Isaacman imposed sweeping program changes that turned Artemis III into an extra practice mission. The agency is pressed to return to the moon quickly as it races China, which is targeting 2030 for its own first moon landing. Artemis III will be the first trip to space for Douglas, who spent years shadowing [USN:L1N40R17V TEXT:"the Artemis II crew"] as a backup. A systems engineering scholar and naval architect, Douglas has a background in the US Coast Guard that taught him how to be adaptable to rapid change, he said. "I learned in the military that the plan only lasts for 10 minutes," he said. "You have expectations, but then you're also ready in the background for change."

item.title: Chanel unveils tiger-print tweed and sheer skirt suits in spring/summer Paris show
item.description: Chanel showed see-through skirts and tiger-print tweed in creative director Matthieu Blazy's spring/summer 2027 collection on Monday as the Parisian fashion house rides a wave of enthusiasm that has helped drive sales even as other luxury brands struggle.
item.dc:creator: Helen Reid
item.content:encoded: Chanel showed see-through skirts and tiger-print tweed in creative director Matthieu Blazy's spring/summer 2027 collection on Monday as the Parisian fashion house rides a wave of enthusiasm that has helped drive sales even as other luxury brands struggle. Since his first collection a year ago, Blazy's designs — injecting youthful glitter and loud colour combinations into the Parisian label's traditional tweed suits — have [USN:L6N41P0WR TEXT:"attracted"] new customers to the brand and kept Chanel stores buzzing with activity. Front-row guests including Dua Lipa, Nicole Kidman, and Pedro Pascal arrived to throngs of cameras in the vast expanse of the Grand Palais. The glass dome roof was hung with a giant moon and a flock of luminescent seagulls, while the floor was laid in a Martian orange-and-green pattern in reflective resin. Models emerged wearing skirt suits in sheer cream or black fabric embroidered with flowers and beads, and in tweed loosened into a wide windowpane print with mesh panels, or reworked in an eye-catching red-and-white tiger print. “Chanel felt as alive as ever,” said Angélique Liautaud, womenswear buying and merchandising director at French department store Printemps. “The masculine wardrobe, the fluid dresses, the lingerie, the liberated body, brought a new sensuality to the house.” Some skirts were sliced into swinging panels, others were shortened into pleated mini-skirts paired with cropped jackets showing the midriff. Hems were frayed or finished with metallic beading. Models sported new versions of the brand's two-tone pumps — in leopard print or tiger print with a cream toe, or baby blue and silver, while sandals were chunky with a large interlocking C logo in gold across the front. Quilted handbags came in black, burgundy, and white with a couple of wild variations in zebra print layered with clashing primary colours. Blazy, known for soundtracking his shows to anthems from the 2000s, ran out to greet the crowd after the finale to the heavy synths of "Gimme More" by Britney Spears.

item.title: Pinterest taps Amazon veteran James Dibbo as CFO

item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Pinterest (PINS.N) said on Monday it has appointed Amazon executive James Dibbo as its chief financial officer, effective October 26. Dibbo, 56, who will succeed Julia Donnelly at Pinterest, has led finance for the e-commerce giant's (AMZN.O) Ads, Prime Video and Amazon MGM Studios businesses among others. item.title: Eagles take drop-in travel approach to London game vs. Jaguars
item.description: Eagles coach Nick Sirianni wants to prepare for the Jaguars at home, delaying travel for Sunday's game in London to Friday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Eagles coach Nick Sirianni wants to prepare for the Jaguars at home, delaying travel for Sunday's game in London to Friday. The travel plan calls for a charter flight scheduled to span around seven hours from Philadelphia to England on Friday, with the Eagles returning immediately after the game Sunday. "We felt like leaving Friday was best for our team, this team, and with the schedule that we have with the weeks coming up," Sirianni said. "At the end of the day, I got to make those decisions and this is the decision I chose, with the help of great people." The wisdom in covering more than 7,000 air miles in a tight window of time -- roughly 48 hours -- is likely to be a hot topic for the Eagles. Because of the time change, the Eagles will land in London on Saturday morning. The potential for jet lag was not a deterrent for Sirianni as the Eagles (2-2) try to rebound from consecutive losses to the Bears and Rams. "We went through all of this," Sirianni said. "We feel like this is giving our team the best chance to win." --Field Level Media

item.title: Euroleague to vote on expansion offers on Tuesday as NBA Europe talks loom
item.description: Euroleague shareholder clubs are unlikely to embrace radical change when they meet this week to consider a 10-year strategic plan, experts said on Monday, in a pivotal week for the sport across the continent with the NBA looking to move in.
item.dc:creator: Ruairidh Barlow
item.content:encoded: Euroleague shareholder clubs are unlikely to embrace radical change when they meet this week to consider a 10-year strategic plan, experts said on Monday, in a pivotal week for the sport across the continent with the NBA looking to move in. Representatives from the 13 permanent Euroleague teams were due in Lake Como on Monday night with a vote on Tuesday on a fundamental ownership shift that would transform those shareholders into franchises and expand the competition from 20 teams to 24. The Euroleague will also evaluate the 14 bids they have received for additional long-term franchise spots, with a maximum of eight to be awarded by ballot. The proposals from the Euroleague are aimed at sustainability and accelerating long-term growth but sceptics remain. "I don't think it really changes what it's on the table today for the 13 shareholders," Lega Basket Serie A President Maurizio Gherardini told Reuters. The strategic plan aims for an aggregate value of the competition and its clubs of €4.3 billion ($4,82 billion) by 2027 and said in a statement on August 25 that projected year-on-year revenue growth had risen to 15% as a result of fresh commercial deals. Despite the positive projections, Real Madrid budgets show net losses in the basketball division each year since the 2021-22 season. Counterparts Barcelona have posted overall net losses for the past three years, and economist Ivan Cabeza told Reuters that the wider Euroleague model was not sustainable. "I find it very hard to see how a business like the Euroleague which has been, is, and very likely will continue to be a money-losing venture, could undergo a radical change," Cabeza said. This could make the NBA Europe project appealing to clubs primarily focused on football, with the North American league widely expected to launch in 2027 - with or without Euroleague's cooperation. The Athletic reported last week that NBA Europe managing director George Aivazoglou and NBA deputy commissioner Mark Tatum held discussions with Paris St Germain, AC Milan and the Spanish duo about becoming member franchises. Media reports said the NBA have submitted a proposal to the Euroleague, which last Friday confirmed to Reuters that talks were ongoing between the two. "If someone came along and said, 'Look, I’ll give you €800 million ($896,88 million) to take over the franchise so you never lose money again', that’s obviously an attractive proposition," said Cabeza, posing a hypothetical for Barcelona and Real Madrid. "It’s appealing because it solves part of your overall debt problem, stops the financial bleeding, and allows you to keep the brand name associated with a partner." Aivazoglou is poised to give an update on their 16-team competition on Thursday in London. Both the NBA and the Euroleague have confirmed they will forge ahead with their own plans for the 2027-28 season if no agreement is found. ($1 = 0.8920 euros)

item.title: Imea mantém projeções da safra 26/27 de soja e milho de MT; vê alta na área de algodão
item.description: O Instituto Mato-grossense de Economia Agropecuária (Imea) manteve em outubro suas estimativas para a safra de soja e milho 2026/27 de Mato Grosso, apesar do atraso inicial da semeadura da oleaginosa provocado pela irregularidade das primeiras chuvas.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: O Instituto Mato-grossense de Economia Agropecuária (Imea) manteve em outubro suas estimativas para a safra de soja e milho 2026/27 de Mato Grosso, apesar do atraso inicial da semeadura da oleaginosa provocado pela irregularidade das primeiras chuvas. O órgão vinculado à federação dos produtores Famato ressaltou que as condições climáticas nos próximos meses serão determinantes para confirmar o potencial produtivo da temporada. As projeções de área, produtividade e produção de soja foram mantidas em 13,05 milhões de hectares, 62,44 sacas de 60 kg por hectare e 48,88 milhões de toneladas, respectivamente. Se confirmada, a projeção de safra do principal Estado produtor brasileiro teria uma queda de cerca de 5% ante o ciclo anterior, baseada em uma produtividade mais baixa, visto que a área teria um leve crescimento. Segundo o instituto, a semeadura começou no Estado, mas segue atrasada em relação às últimas safras devido à irregularidade das precipitações e à cautela dos produtores diante do risco de interrupção das chuvas após o plantio. "Até o momento, contudo, o atraso ocorre em uma fase ainda inicial da implantação das lavouras e não apresenta magnitude suficiente para justificar alterações nas estimativas de produtividade e produção", afirmou o Imea em relatório mensal. O instituto destacou ainda que o foco do mercado passa a ser o comportamento climático entre novembro e dezembro, período crucial para o desenvolvimento das lavouras, em um ano sob influência do El Niño. "A eventual ocorrência de veranicos, sobretudo se coincidir com fases mais sensíveis da cultura, como florescimento e formação de vagens, poderá limitar o potencial produtivo", alertou. Para o milho 2026/27, cuja área plantada pode sofrer influência do ritmo de plantio da soja e da definição da janela ideal de plantio da segunda safra, o Imea também manteve suas projeções. A área destinada ao cereal permaneceu estimada em 7,48 milhões de hectares, avanço de 0,59% ante a temporada 2025/26. A produtividade foi mantida em 119,64 sacas por hectare, queda de 8,05% na comparação anual, enquanto a produção seguiu projetada em 53,68 milhões de toneladas, recuo de 7,50%. O instituto afirmou que a demanda doméstica aquecida continua sustentando a atratividade econômica da cultura no Estado. ALGODÃO Em sua primeira estimativa para a safra de algodão 2026/27, o Imea projetou aumento de 3,8% da área cultivada em Mato Grosso, para 1,43 milhão de hectares, impulsionado pelos preços mais atrativos da pluma. "O momento atual de preços mais atrativos da pluma tem motivado o investimento na cultura para a próxima temporada", afirmou o instituto. A produção, entretanto, poderia recuar 2,4% ante o ciclo anterior, para 2,73 milhões de toneladas da pluma, uma vez que o Imea vê produtividades mais baixas. O instituto ponderou, porém, que as projeções ainda estão sujeitas às condições climáticas da temporada, incluindo possíveis efeitos do fenômeno El Niño e eventuais atrasos na colheita da soja, que podem postergar a semeadura do algodão de segunda safra e elevar a exposição da cultura ao risco climático.

item.title: New Zealand third quarter business confidence jumps, says think tank
item.description: New Zealand's business confidence rose in the third quarter even as fuel prices increased and geopolitics remained a headwind for the country, a private think tank said on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: New Zealand's business confidence rose in the third quarter even as fuel prices increased and geopolitics remained a headwind for the country, a private think tank said on Tuesday. A net 43% of firms surveyed expected general business conditions to improve compared with 8% optimism in the previous quarter, the New Zealand Institute of Economic Research's quarterly survey of business opinion showed. The survey was undertaken from September 9 to 28 and coincided with a surge in fuel prices amid a reescalation of the conflict between the US and Iran. “These recent developments highlight ongoing volatility and uncertainty in global oil supply and prices, but the impact on sentiment appears muted for now,” NZIER said in a statement. On a seasonally adjusted basis, 40% expected business conditions to improve versus 14% optimism recorded in the previous period. The survey's measure of capacity utilization rose to 91.0%, from the previous quarter's 90.8%. “There is once again that divergence between what firms experience, which is still fairly weak activity, and what they’re expecting for the next quarter, which generally is one of an improvement ahead,” Christina Leung, principal economist at NZIER, said at a press conference. NZIER said in a statement that the stabilisation in costs and pricing indicators in the latest survey suggests a modest risk of higher fuel prices flowing through to broader inflation pressures. Leung said NZIER does not believe there needs to be any further cash rate hikes this year. New Zealand’s central bank increased the cash rate by 25 basis points in [USN:L1N44U036 TEXT:"September"] to 2.75% and signaled more tightening ahead, but stressed any further moves would be measured as it warned of mounting risks to the economic outlook.

item.title: L'Oreal explores unloading chemical-related liabilities, WSJ reports
item.description: L'Oreal has engaged restructuring advisers to explore options for rising US legal liabilities linked to its use of talc and other chemical ingredients in some of its cosmetic products, the Wall Street Journal reported on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: L'Oreal (OREP.PA) has engaged restructuring advisers to explore options for rising US legal liabilities linked to its use of talc and other chemical ingredients in some of its cosmetic products, the Wall Street Journal reported on Monday. L'Oreal's US unit is working with restructuring counsel Weil Gotshal & Manges and investment bank Ducera Partners to address lawsuits from individuals alleging the talc products caused illness, the Journal said, citing people familiar with the matter. L'Oreal, Weil Gotshal & Manges and Ducera did not immediately respond to requests for comment. The cosmetics maker is also facing thousands of lawsuits that allege its hair relaxer products could cause cancer in women. Arizona [USN:L6N45313S TEXT:"sued"] L'Oreal and its US subsidiary in September, alleging the cosmetics company hid evidence that the products could cause cancer. L'Oreal USA has previously said the company is confident in the safety of its products and believes those claims are without legal or scientific merit.

Today's Talking Points: Brazil That rumbling you feel beneath your feet is the first tremors of what could be a political earthquake in Brazil. Right-wing candidate Flavio Bolsonaro, son of former hard-right President [USN:S0N42U07U TEXT:"Jair"] Bolsonaro, did much better than expected in the first round of voting in Sunday's presidential election, and from a financial markets viewpoint at least, the [USN:L1N45R09E TEXT:"verdict"] is clear — the sizzling rally in Brazilian assets on Monday says it all. Incumbent [USN:L1N45R0KI TEXT:"Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva"], the left-wing veteran going for his fourth non-consecutive term, is considering tapping Vice President Geraldo Alckmin to be his next finance minister if re-elected, in a bid to bolster his fiscal credibility and win over centrist voters. But it may be too little too late — online betting markets are pointing to an 83% likelihood that Bolsonaro wins in the second round of voting. Europe To France, Italy and Germany last week, investors can add Spain to their European political risk watch-list, after Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez called a snap election following nationwide protests over housing. It's a high-stakes gamble for Sanchez, whose Socialist Party trails in nearly every opinion poll. Defeat would spell the end of one of Europe's last remaining left-leaning governments at a time when the far right is making unprecedented gains across the region. Spain's political turmoil isn't tied to fiscal concerns like other countries — Spain is one of the fastest-growing economies in the euro zone, its deficit is around 2-2.5% of GDP, and yield spreads are under relative control. Still, markets are twitchy — Spanish yields rose 5 bps and the euro slumped to a fresh 17-month low around $1.12. Dollar In G10 FX, the big beneficiary of deepening political and bond market uncertainty sweeping, to varying degrees, across Europe, the UK and Japan is the dollar. The US doesn't have its political, debt or bond market troubles to seek either, of course. But to coin an old FX market adage, the greenback is once again proving to be the cleanest dirty shirt in the laundry. This isn't what President Trump or Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent really want. They would prefer a weaker dollar that is more competitive in the global marketplace, which would theoretically help boost US exports and narrow the trade deficit that Trump says is a result of America being "ripped off" by the rest of the world. On the other hand, a stronger dollar helps suppress imported price pressures and the need for tighter monetary policy. Now that's music to Trump's ears. What could move markets tomorrow? item.title: Bengals WR Tee Higgins (adductor) day-to-day, could play Week 5
item.description: While Ja'Marr Chase is in the league's concussion protocol, his longtime receiving mate in Cincinnati, Tee Higgins, may not have to miss game action following his adductor injury Sunday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: While Ja'Marr Chase is in the league's concussion protocol, his longtime receiving mate in Cincinnati, Tee Higgins, may not have to miss game action following his adductor injury Sunday. Bengals coach Zac Taylor said Monday that Higgins is day-to-day, and he didn't rule out the possibility that Higgins could play Week 5 at the Miami Dolphins. "(We'll) see where he is at this week," Taylor told reporters. Higgins injured his adductor following a toe-tapping sideline grab late in Cincinnati's 22-17 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. He left briefly and returned for one play on the Bengals' final drive but was unable to continue. Higgins reeled in 11 receptions for 157 yards. The 27-year-old has 25 receptions for 401 yards and one touchdown in four games this season for Cincinnati (2-2). His production Sunday was critical after Chase, 26, was ruled out with a concussion after his head hit the turf early in the second quarter. Chase, 26, has 21 receptions for 212 yards and three touchdowns over four games this season. In six NFL seasons, all with the Bengals, the five-time Pro Bowl selection has 541 receptions for 7,049 yards and 57 touchdowns. In his seventh season in Cincinnati, Higgins has 414 catches for 5,842 yards and 46 touchdowns. He earned his first Pro Bowl selection last year, posting a career-high 11 touchdowns. --Field Level Media

item.title: Cuba y EEUU mantienen "canales de comunicación", pero no hay negociaciones: diplomática
item.description: Cuba y Estados Unidos han mantenido "canales de comunicación", pero no hay una negociación formal, dijo a Reuters la máxima representante diplomática de La Habana en Washington, mientras el Gobierno del presidente Donald Trump prosigue con su campaña de presión contra la isla gobernada por el régimen comunista.
item.dc:creator: Matt Spetalnick
item.content:encoded: Cuba y Estados Unidos han mantenido "canales de comunicación", pero no hay una negociación formal, dijo a Reuters la máxima representante diplomática de La Habana en Washington, mientras el Gobierno del presidente Donald Trump prosigue con su campaña de presión contra la isla gobernada por el régimen comunista. En una entrevista concedida el lunes, Lianys Torres Rivera, encargada de negocios de la embajada en Washington, dijo que Cuba sigue abierta a un diálogo "respetuoso", pero que "no es ingenua" respecto a las amenazas del presidente Donald Trump y ha intensificado los preparativos para defenderse de cualquier acción militar estadounidense. Los últimos contactos diplomáticos entre Estados Unidos y Cuba han consistido en reuniones, así como en llamadas telefónicas y mensajes de WhatsApp, pero ninguna de las dos partes ha avanzado hacia una agenda de negociación ni hacia la reanudación de las conversaciones oficiales, señaló. "Lo que tenemos con Estados Unidos son canales de comunicación", dijo Torres Rivera, que no quiso dar detalles sobre los plazos, los temas y los participantes. Su descripción de las comunicaciones parece distar de la afirmación de Trump el mes pasado ante las Naciones Unidas de que el secretario de Estado, Marco Rubio, se encontraba "en plenas negociaciones" con La Habana. Trump también calificó a Cuba de "Estado fallido" y predijo que su Gobierno caería. La delegación cubana abandonó la sala en señal de protesta. Trump ha declarado abiertamente que su objetivo es cambiar de forma radical el Gobierno de Cuba. En respuesta a las preguntas de Reuters, un funcionario estadounidense no dio detalles sobre los contactos diplomáticos, pero dijo, bajo condición de anonimato: "Estados Unidos está dispuesto a abrir un nuevo capítulo en la relación (…) Lo único que se interpone en el camino hacia un futuro mejor son aquellos que controlan Cuba para su propio beneficio a costa del pueblo cubano". Torres Rivera dijo que la "línea roja" de Cuba sigue siendo que La Habana no está dispuesta a negociar ningún cambio en su sistema político, y considera que las exigencias de Trump de que se destituya a los dirigentes cubanos constituyen una violación de la soberanía.

item.title: France come from behind to thrash Belgium 4-1
item.description: France came from a goal down to beat Belgium 4-1 in their Nations League Group A1 meeting at the Stade de France on Monday, while Italy secured a 3-1 win over Turkey, their third consecutive match without a loss.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: France came from a goal down to beat Belgium 4-1 in their Nations League Group A1 meeting at the Stade de France on Monday, while Italy secured a 3-1 win over Turkey, their third consecutive match without a loss. Zinedine Zidane secured his first home win in charge, three days after a 1-1 draw against Italy, thanks to his substitutes. Belgium's Dodi Lukebakio put the visitors ahead in the 35th minute, but Desire Doue, Rayan Cherki and Michael Olise, all on the bench at kickoff, turned the match on its head in the final 15 minutes. Doue levelled with a left-footed shot from the edge of the box in the 77th minute. Four minutes later, Cherki put his side in front, finishing from an Olise cross. Olise then completed a brace from close range just before and during stoppage time. "That's football, that's what we love. There were difficulties, but that's part of the game, part of the kinds of matches you can have," Zidane told TF1. "It's good to put things right, and that's what we did with an extraordinary second half. We were just missing that final few metres in the first half, but then we turned the match around, it was good." Belgium took the lead when Lukebakio broke clear of a defence that was stepping up for offside to latch onto a long pass from Romeo Lavia, before scoring in a one-on-one with Guillaume Restes, who was earning his first cap. The 2018 World Cup winners, playing without captain Kylian Mbappe, controlled possession but failed to create chances against a packed defensive block, making it an eighth consecutive match without scoring in the first half. Then Olise and Cherki came off the bench on the hour mark, 12 minutes before Doue, and France became more dangerous. "We played well at the end; in the first half it was difficult against their low block. After that we kept going and it was good in the end," Olise told TF1. "It's a team effort, Zidane brings ideas and we follow them. We're going to keep going like this." After Maarten Vandevoordt, who was also winning his first cap, denied efforts from Bradley Barcola, Esteban Lepaul, Olise and Cherki, the Belgian goalkeeper was unable to stop Doue's strike. The Paris St Germain winger levelled with a left-footed shot across goal from the edge of the box. Four minutes later, Olise began his masterclass. He first delivered a cross for Cherki to score before completing a quickfire double from close range within three minutes to give France a resounding victory. Italy's victory over Turkey came with Gianluca Scamacca, Riccardo Calafiori and Pio Esposito scoring, while Aral Simsir had earlier equalised just after the hour mark. Scamacca scored the opener with a close‑range volley that hit the crossbar before crossing the line. Simsir levelled at the far post at the end of a beautiful team move from the Turks, but three minutes later Calafiori's header from a Nicolo Barella free kick restored Italy's lead. Esposito scored the final goal after Issa Doumbia and Alessandro Romano had both failed to convert. "Even though we had made a lot of changes, there was fatigue all around, and we struggled a bit," coach Roberto Mancini told RAI. "But we did well to score, and then to score again right after they equalised." France sit top with 10 points, three ahead of Italy and four clear of Belgium. Turkey are bottom with four defeats from four matches.

item.title: Ravens optimistic QB Lamar Jackson ankle injury isn't 'crazy long-term'
item.description: Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson is not ruled out for Week 5, a Sunday night matchup with the Atlanta Falcons, but Baltimore is bracing for his absence to stretch beyond the second half of a Week 4 win.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson is not ruled out for Week 5, a Sunday night matchup with the Atlanta Falcons, but Baltimore is bracing for his absence to stretch beyond the second half of a Week 4 win. Ravens coach Jesse Minter said it's too early to know what Jackson's status could be for this week. Jackson injured his left ankle and wore a protective boot out of the stadium on Sunday night after sitting out the second half of a 24-18 victory over the Tennessee Titans. "I really don't think it's going to be crazy long-term, but we'll see what happens," Minter said. The Ravens (3-1) share the AFC North lead with the Cleveland Browns (3-1), who will host Baltimore on Oct. 18. Jackson's status won't be updated until Wednesday afternoon, Minter said. The Ravens would start Tyler Huntley against the Falcons if Jackson isn't available. Huntley completed 8 of 9 passes for 63 yards in the second half to steer Baltimore past Tennessee. Minter said Monday he didn't "know the chances yet" that Huntley could be in line to make his 12th start with the Ravens. He's 5-6 as a spot starter with Baltimore. "We're still gathering a lot of the information and the imaging and things like that, just dealing with a little bit of an ankle and we'll kind of see where that shakes out," Minter said of Jackson's status. "Full trust and confidence in him that when it's ready to roll that we'll roll and go from there." --Field Level Media

item.title: UK author and politician Jeffrey Archer dies aged 86
item.description: Jeffrey Archer, the best-selling British novelist and former politician who was jailed for lying in a high-profile libel case, has died aged 86, his publisher HarperCollins said on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Jeffrey Archer, the best-selling British novelist and former politician who was jailed for lying in a high-profile libel case, has died aged 86, his publisher HarperCollins said on Monday. Archer sold over 300 million copies worldwide and was known for pacy thrillers like his 1976 debut "Not a Penny More, Not a Penny Less" and "Kane & Abel", with his final novel Adam and Eve due to be published this month. He was also a prominent Conservative politician, who briefly served as a lawmaker before becoming a senior party official under prime minister Margaret Thatcher in the mid-1980s. But Archer suffered a very public downfall when he was convicted of perjury and perverting the course of justice in 2001, being sentenced to four years' imprisonment. Kate Elton, HarperCollins' UK CEO and Archer's editor, said in a statement: "We're all devastated to have lost a writer who has brought joy to generations of readers - and a true friend."

item.title: Nvidia-backed Reflection unveils first AI model to take on Chinese open models
item.description: Nvidia-backed Reflection AI debuted its first open-weight model named Beam on Monday, as the startup aims to compete with lower-cost Chinese models such as DeepSeek and Kimi in coding and agentic tasks.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Nvidia-backed (NVDA.O) Reflection AI debuted its first open-weight model named Beam on Monday, as the startup aims to compete with lower-cost Chinese models such as DeepSeek and Kimi in coding and agentic tasks. Reflection said Beam is competitive with Chinese AI startup Z.ai's GLM‑5.2 and is closing in on Qwen3.8‑Max on coding and agentic tasks. Here are some details: The startup said that Beam contains 501 billion total parameters, or variables that determine how an AI system processes information, but activates only 23 billion for each task to make the model faster and cheaper to run by using only part of its network for each task. Comparatively, Z.ai's GLM-5.2 has about 744 billion total parameters with 40 billion active parameters. The launch comes as [USN:L6N44911H TEXT:"US tech firms are trying"] to fend off competition from Chinese open-weight models that are cheaper, more customizable and capable of generating code nearly as well as leading models from OpenAI and Anthropic. Founded in 2024 by former DeepMind researchers Misha Laskin and Ioannis Antonoglou, Reflection develops tools that automate software development, a fast-growing use case for AI. Earlier this year, Reflection [USN:L4N42U1H9 TEXT:"signed a deal with SpaceX"] for additional computing capacity at the Elon Musk-led company's Colossus 2 data center.

item.title: Nova York declara estado de emergência devido a surto de sarampo
item.description: A governadora de Nova York, Kathy Hochul, declarou nesta segunda-feira estado de emergência em todo o Estado devido a um surto de sarampo, a primeira declaração do tipo feita por um Estado norte-americano desde que os casos começaram a aumentar, em 2025.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A governadora de Nova York, Kathy Hochul, declarou nesta segunda-feira estado de emergência em todo o Estado devido a um surto de sarampo, a primeira declaração do tipo feita por um Estado norte-americano desde que os casos começaram a aumentar, em 2025. O Estado também ampliou o número de profissionais de saúde autorizados a administrar vacinas contra sarampo, caxumba e rubéola devido ao aumento de casos em comunidades rurais. Nova York registrou 108 casos de sarampo neste ano até 3 de outubro -- 92 deles de 15 de julho ao início de outubro -- em comunidades rurais com baixa cobertura vacinal em 18 condados, bem acima dos níveis anuais típicos, de acordo com o decreto da governadora. O Estado vizinho da Pensilvânia está enfrentando um surto de rápida propagação, com 977 casos e cinco mortes até 2 de outubro, principalmente em condados rurais que fazem fronteira com Nova York, segundo o decreto. O decreto permite que enfermeiros registrados solicitem exames para suspeita de sarampo e que farmacêuticos vacinem crianças a partir de dois anos de idade. Também exige que todas as vacinações contra sarampo, caxumba e rubéola sejam registradas nos sistemas de imunização estaduais ou da cidade de Nova York em até 72 horas, dispensando o consentimento de adultos para tal comunicação. A vacinação em si ainda requer o consentimento do paciente ou de um responsável legal. O estado de emergência entrou em vigor nesta segunda-feira e vai até 4 de novembro.

item.title: Nueva York declara estado de emergencia por brote de sarampión
item.description: La gobernadora de Nueva York, Kathy Hochul, declaró el lunes emergencia por catástrofe en todo el estado a raíz de un brote de sarampión, después de que se detectaron 108 casos en el año.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La gobernadora de Nueva York, Kathy Hochul, declaró el lunes emergencia por catástrofe en todo el estado a raíz de un brote de sarampión, después de que se detectaron 108 casos en el año. Desde el 15 de julio se han contabilizado 92 casos en 18 condados de Nueva York, mientras que Pensilvania ha tenido 977, muchos de ellos en condados rurales situados en la frontera con Nueva York, indicó la gobernadora. El decreto exige que todas las vacunaciones contra el sarampión, las paperas y la rubéola se comuniquen a los registros del estado o de la ciudad de Nueva York en 72 horas. La orden permite a las enfermeras solicitar pruebas en caso de sospecha de sarampión y a los farmacéuticos vacunar a niños a partir de los dos años. La vacunación en sí misma sigue requiriendo el consentimiento del paciente o de un tutor legal. La medida de emergencia entró en vigor el lunes y estará vigente hasta el 4 de noviembre.

item.title: Dezenas de pessoas estão em quarentena na Sibéria após morte de funcionária de laboratório de instituto sobre peste
item.description: Uma funcionária de laboratório de um instituto de pesquisa sobre a peste na Sibéria adoeceu e faleceu em circunstâncias não reveladas, levando as autoridades a colocarem dezenas de pessoas em quarentena e fazendo com que a chefe do órgão regulador de saúde da Rússia se deslocasse à região de Irkutsk.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Osborn
item.content:encoded: Uma funcionária de laboratório de um instituto de pesquisa sobre a peste na Sibéria adoeceu e faleceu em circunstâncias não reveladas, levando as autoridades a colocarem dezenas de pessoas em quarentena e fazendo com que a chefe do órgão regulador de saúde da Rússia se deslocasse à região de Irkutsk. A morte gerou temores relacionados à saúde pública nas redes sociais, mas as autoridades afirmaram nesta segunda-feira que a situação estava sob controle. A Organização Mundial da Saúde (OMS) afirmou que, com base nas informações disponíveis, “o risco à saúde pública para a população em geral parece ser baixo”. Novas avaliações de risco serão realizadas assim que mais informações forem divulgadas, informou a organização. O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, disse que a morte era um “grande problema para a Rússia” e se ofereceu para ajudar Moscou a lidar com a situação. “Vamos ajudar”, disse Trump. “Para quem tiver esse tipo de problema, estamos sempre dispostos a ajudar.” O secretário de Estado dos EUA, Marco Rubio, disse que Washington estava acompanhando de perto a situação. A peste é endêmica na Sibéria, local do primeiro surto humano pré-histórico conhecido, já que a bactéria que a causa, a Yersinia pestis, está presente entre os pequenos mamíferos selvagens em suas vastas áreas e em suas pulgas. É raro que russos adoeçam com a peste, no entanto, embora casos em outras partes do mundo — notadamente na África — ocorram todos os anos. A peste se apresenta em três formas que afetam diferentes partes do corpo. A peste pneumônica, uma infecção dos pulmões, faz com que o paciente espalhe gotículas infecciosas pelo ar ao tossir. Se diagnosticada rapidamente, pode ser tratada com antibióticos. Mas, se não for tratada, pode ser fatal em um a seis dias. A mídia local identificou a mulher como Darya Shipilova, funcionária do Instituto de Pesquisa Antipeste de Irkutsk da Sibéria e do Extremo Oriente. Houve relatos contraditórios sobre como e onde a funcionária do laboratório, cuja idade foi informada como 28 anos, havia adoecido, mas as autoridades afirmaram que ela havia morrido de pneumonia de origem ainda não determinada. AUTORIDADES DIZEM QUE NÃO FORAM RELATADOS NOVOS CASOS E QUE TODOS OS CONTATOS FORAM RASTREADOS O órgão regulador de saúde da Rússia, Rospotrebnadzor, informou à mídia estatal que o instituto não havia encontrado evidências de nenhum acidente envolvendo o manuseio de patógenos, após rumores se espalharem nas redes sociais de que a mulher teria deixado cair um tubo de ensaio contendo bactérias vivas. No entanto, Anna Popova, chefe da Rospotrebnadzor, voou para a Sibéria para uma reunião de emergência no fim de semana. De acordo com reportagens da mídia russa, cerca de 200 pessoas que tiveram contato com a mulher falecida foram colocadas em quarentena, partes do hospital na cidade de Shelekhov, onde ela faleceu, foram isoladas e uma fábrica de alumínio orientou seus funcionários a usarem máscaras. A Rospotrebnadzor, em comunicado posterior citado pela agência de notícias Tass, informou que autoridades da região de Irkutsk haviam identificado dois casos de Covid e dois casos de rinovírus entre as pessoas que estiveram em contato com ela. Nenhum outro caso de doenças infecciosas foi registrado. As autoridades pediram que as pessoas mantivessem a calma e afirmaram que não havia evidências de que a morte da mulher estivesse relacionada ao seu trabalho. Igor Kobzev, governador da região de Irkutsk, afirmou em comunicado que ela havia falecido de “pneumonia de etiologia desconhecida”, acrescentando: “É importante ressaltar que, nos últimos dias, não foram identificados novos casos de funcionários do Instituto Antipeste que procurassem atendimento médico.” Ele afirmou que a situação estava sob controle e que todos os contatos conhecidos da mulher falecida haviam sido identificados, examinados e colocados sob supervisão médica.

item.title: Air taxi maker Joby Aero owes $116.9 million in trade secrets case, US jury says
item.description: A federal jury in Tampa, Florida, has awarded airplane component maker Aerosonic nearly $116.9 million after finding that air taxi company Joby Aero broke a confidentiality agreement and misused trade secrets related to Aerosonic aircraft sensors.
item.dc:creator: Blake Brittain
item.content:encoded: A federal jury in Tampa, Florida, has awarded airplane component maker Aerosonic nearly $116.9 million after finding that air taxi company Joby Aero broke a confidentiality agreement and misused trade secrets related to Aerosonic aircraft sensors. The jury in a verdict on Friday found that Joby owes Aerosonic more than $68 million for breaching the companies' non-disclosure agreement and more than $48 million for willfully misappropriating trade secrets related to its air data probes A Joby spokesperson said on Monday that the company strongly disagrees with the verdict and intends to "vigorously pursue all available post-trial and appellate remedies" The emerging air-taxi market, led by companies including Joby and backed by major automakers, airlines and investors, has spawned a [USN:L4N45O19W TEXT:"string"] of trade-secret and patent disputes Clearwater, Florida-based Aerosonic sued Joby last year, alleging Joby stole its secrets after Aerosonic sold Joby air data probes and discussed supplying more for its electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft Santa Cruz, California-based Joby denied the allegations and countersued Aerosonic for allegedly selling it defective probes The jury also rejected Joby's countersuit on Friday The case is Aerosonic LLC v. Joby Aero Inc, US District Court for the Middle District of Florida, No. 8:25-cv-00554 For Aerosonic: Todd Tucker of Calfee, Halter & Griswold For Joby: Naveen Modi of Paul Hastings Read more: [USN:L4N45O19W TEXT:"US court trims Joby's trade-secret case against Archer Aviation"]

item.title: Data centre operator DayOne reveals revenue surge in US IPO filing
item.description: Data center operator DayOne Data Centers filed for an initial public offering in the United States on Monday, testing investor appetite for data-center listings amid challenging market conditions.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Data center operator DayOne Data Centers filed for an initial public offering in the United States on Monday, testing investor appetite for data-center listings amid challenging market conditions. The company posted a net loss of $77.2 million on revenue of $512 million for the six months ended June 30, compared with a loss of $12.6 million on revenue of $151.5 million a year earlier. The filing comes as surging bond yields and elevated interest rates cloud the outlook for the fall IPO market, prompting several major listings to be [USN:L6N45L0OG TEXT:"postponed"]. Data centers have also come under scrutiny over their heavy use of electricity, water and land, with communities raising concerns about their impact on power grids, utility bills and local resources. The Singapore-based company develops and operates data centers for cloud-computing and AI customers, providing space, power, cooling and connectivity, primarily under long-term contracts. DayOne operates across Asia-Pacific and Europe, including Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand, Hong Kong, Japan, Finland and Spain, according to its filing. Shanghai-based GDS Holdings set up GDS International in Singapore in 2022, which was rebranded as DayOne in January 2025 following its separation from the parent company. The company has not disclosed the size of the offering, although Reuters [USN:L4N3Z90C5 TEXT:"reported"] in February that it was aiming to raise as much as $5 billion at a potential valuation of $20 billion. DayOne plans to use the IPO proceeds to develop and construct new data-center projects and for working capital and other general corporate purposes. Morgan Stanley, J.P. Morgan, BofA Securities and Citigroup are among the underwriters for the offering. DayOne plans to list its American depositary shares on the Nasdaq under the symbol “DODC.”

item.title: Conservation group calls for moratorium on AI data centers on US public lands
item.description: Conservation group The Wilderness Society on Monday called for a moratorium on artificial intelligence data centers on federal lands, citing concerns over water use, electricity demand, wildlife habitat and public access.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Conservation group The Wilderness Society on Monday called for a moratorium on artificial intelligence data centers on federal lands, citing concerns over water use, electricity demand, wildlife habitat and public access. The call comes as the Trump administration is considering permits for several data center developments on lands managed by the Bureau of Land Management, according to federal land records. US President Donald Trump has sought to expand a range of industries on public lands, including mining and oil and gas Trump has championed rapid expansion of AI infrastructure and data centers, describing them as critical to economic growth and technological competitiveness. But the industry has increasingly faced local opposition The Wilderness Society said public lands should remain focused on recreation, conservation and public access, and called for a pause before large-scale industrial development tied to AI is allowed on federally managed lands BLM officials did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The agency manages about a tenth of America's land base, primarily in Western states

item.title: Peso mexicano recupera terreno, pero se mantiene por encima de 18 por dólar
item.description: El peso mexicano avanzó el lunes por segunda jornada consecutiva, mientras los mercados centran su atención en las minutas de las reuniones más recientes de la Reserva Federal de Estados Unidos (Fed) y del Banco de México, que podrían ofrecer nuevas señales sobre la brecha monetaria entre ambos países.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El peso mexicano avanzó el lunes por segunda jornada consecutiva, mientras los mercados centran su atención en las minutas de las reuniones más recientes de la [USN:L1N4580T6 TEXT:"Reserva Federal"] de Estados Unidos (Fed) y del [USN:L6N45G177 TEXT:"Banco de México"], que podrían ofrecer nuevas señales sobre la brecha monetaria entre ambos países. La expectativa de un menor diferencial de tasas entre Estados Unidos y México ha presionado recientemente a la moneda, ante el temor de que disminuya el atractivo de las operaciones de [USN:L1N45L0OH TEXT:"carry trade"], que buscan aprovechar los mayores rendimientos de los activos locales y durante años han apuntalado al peso. * La divisa mexicana operaba en 18.0845 por dólar en la recta final de los negocios, con una apreciación de un 0.33% en su segunda sesión de ganancias. El jueves, llegó a debilitarse hasta [USN:L1N45N0ZE TEXT:"18.4330 unidades"], un nivel no visto desde noviembre de 2025. * El repunte de la moneda ocurrió en medio de un [USN:L6N45R11S TEXT:"fortalecimiento global del dólar"], a medida que el euro se hundió, y una caída de los [USN:L6N45R0XX TEXT:"precios del petróleo"], tras un incremento de las exportaciones de crudo desde Oriente Medio. * Las actas de la [USN:L1N4580T6 TEXT:"Fed"], previstas para el miércoles, llegarán después de que [USN:L6N45O0QK TEXT:"datos laborales"] de Estados Unidos divulgados el viernes redujeron las expectativas de otro aumento de tasas en octubre, tras el ajuste aplicado en septiembre. * En México, los operadores esperan para el jueves las minutas del [USN:L6N45G177 TEXT:"banco central"] y datos de [USN:L1N45Q009 TEXT:"inflación de septiembre"]. * De acuerdo con analistas técnicos de Monex Grupo Financiero, el mercado muestra señales de una menor presión compradora para el tipo de cambio. "Consideramos que podría entrar en una fase de consolidación lateral con sesgo bajista, en tanto se mantenga contenida la demanda por coberturas cambiarias y activos de refugio, principalmente en dólares", dijo la firma en un reporte. * La bolsa mexicana también cerró con ganancias por segunda jornada. Les siguieron los papeles de la gigante de telecomunicaciones América Móvil (AMXB.MX) que sumaron un 3.77%, a 20.09 pesos. * En el mercado secundario de deuda, el rendimiento del bono gubernamental a 10 años ascendió tres puntos básicos, a un 9.54%. item.title: In road trip finale, Panthers aim to spoil Kings' home opener
item.description: Before the Florida Panthers get to feel the energy inside Amerant Bank Arena for the first time this season, they'll have to experience another team's home opener Tuesday night when they visit the Los Angeles Kings to conclude a season-opening four-game road trip.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Before the Florida Panthers get to feel the energy inside Amerant Bank Arena for the first time this season, they'll have to experience another team's home opener Tuesday night when they visit the Los Angeles Kings to conclude a season-opening four-game road trip. They opened the new campaign with a 1-0 overtime win against the Carolina Hurricanes on Sept. 29, then lost 4-3 in overtime to the Sharks in San Jose's season opener Thursday. Florida faced another young, fast team riled up for their first home game Sunday and again rallied late, pushing the Anaheim Ducks to overtime before losing 3-2. "Anytime you do three home openers in a row, it's obviously tough," Florida forward Carter Verhaeghe said. "It probably builds character for us and a good challenge for us, obviously. Other teams (are) going to come out, bring their best, and be skating and flying around." A lot has changed with the Panthers' roster since they headed out west. Team captain Aleksander Barkov suffered a leg injury against the Sharks and was placed on long-term injured reserve. The veteran center reportedly will miss 10 to 12 weeks. Brad Marchand recovered sooner than expected from offseason surgery, and the veteran forward took the ice against the Ducks, scoring a late 6-on-5 goal to send the game to overtime. "It was a bit of a rude awakening," Marchand said. "The speed of the game and the intensity definitely ramped up at times, but it was great to be back out there. It's going to take some time to get the timing and everything back, and conditioning back, but it was incredible being back out there and being part of the team again." Marchand played on a line with Brady Tkachuk and Sam Reinhart, feeling their potential as the game wore on, even if he felt a step slow. "We had a few looks, but it's tough for those guys," said Marchand, who had been out since March 6. "They know I'm just getting back, and it's been almost six months since I played a game and only been skating for a month now. "So, I kind of bring them down a little bit, just with my timing and the speed and all of that, so we're working through that together. But when I get back there, up to speed, we have great potential to be a really good line." The Kings are still looking for their first win after dropping their season opener 8-4 to the Colorado Avalanche in Denver on Wednesday and losing 5-4 in overtime in San Jose on Saturday. "It's tough," Kings coach Peter Laviolette said. "We're chasing the game a little bit. I thought that there was a ton of fight in the end (against San Jose). I really liked the way we played the overtime, and I hate the result. So, lots of things that we did well but, you know, we're still early in the season. We're working on things out there as well to get better at." Forward Quinton Byfield thought the Kings improved in preventing odd-man rushes against the Sharks, and they went 2-for-3 on the power play after going 0-for-4 against the Avalanche. "Our power play wasn't great the first game, so scoring two this game really kind of boosts it," Byfield said. --Field Level Media

item.title: Centalion acquires Haynesville natural gas assets from Silver Hill
item.description: Centalion Group said on Monday it acquired upstream and midstream natural gas assets in Texas and Louisiana's Haynesville region from Texas-based private shale company Silver Hill Energy Partners.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Centalion Group said on Monday it acquired upstream and midstream natural gas assets in Texas and Louisiana's Haynesville region from Texas-based private shale company Silver Hill Energy Partners. The commodities trader, formerly known as Gunvor, [USN:L1N45O096 TEXT:"rebranded"] as Centalion Group last week and said it planned to redomicile its corporate headquarters to Singapore from Cyprus. A Centalion spokesperson said the company's Haynesville platform, comprising the Post Oak and Silver Hill assets, has an enterprise value of about $2 billion. Reuters [USN:L1N44M0TQ TEXT:"reported"] in August that Centalion was in talks to acquire the Silver Hill assets in a deal valued at between $1.2 billion and $1.5 billion, citing sources familiar with the matter. The assets have current net natural gas production of about 300 million cubic feet per day (MMcfd) and the portfolio includes about 72,000 net acres in the Haynesville and Bossier development areas. "The rationale is for us to have a footprint in a basin that is the pivot point between domestic and export markets, allowing us to capture and create value from that optionality," the spokesperson added.

item.title: Queda no percentual de Flávio não indica erro; proporção muda conforme total de votos
item.description: Um vídeo que circula nas redes sociais alega que houve um problema na apuração da eleição presidencial neste domingo porque o candidato Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) teve uma redução no percentual apesar de ter somado mais votos do que seu principal adversário, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), entre duas atualizações da contagem.
item.dc:creator: Reuters Fact Check
item.content:encoded: Um vídeo que circula nas redes sociais alega que houve um problema na apuração da eleição presidencial neste domingo porque o candidato Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) teve uma redução no percentual apesar de ter somado mais votos do que seu principal adversário, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT), entre duas atualizações da contagem. No entanto, a variação ocorre porque o percentual nada mais é que a proporção de votos para cada candidato dentro do total de votos válidos, e estes números mudam ao longo da apuração. “O Flávio saiu de 12 milhões para 14 milhões e cacetada, foram 2 milhões de votos que ele ganhou, mas, mesmo assim, abaixou o percentual dele. Agora, o Lula estava com 10 milhões e foi para 11 milhões, foi 1 milhão só de votos. Como o Lula estava com 40,82% e subiu para 40,97%, e o Flávio ganhou mais de 2 milhões de votos e a porcentagem dele abaixou? Alguém explica o que aconteceu, porque eu não estou entendendo”, alega um influenciador no vídeo, que circula no Instagram . Enquanto fala, o homem mostra duas telas da transmissão da CNN Brasil deste domingo. Uma delas, das 18h23min , exibe os resultados com 21,96% das urnas apuradas: Flávio – 12.915.526 votos (51,07%) Lula – 10.324.360 (40,82%) Augusto Cury (Avante) – 743.675 (2,94%) Ronaldo Caiado (PSD) – 602.335 (2,38%) A outra, das 18h25min , mostra as parciais com 24,45% da totalização: Flávio – 14.344.471 (50,94%) Lula – 11.536.137 (40,97%) Cury – 827.940 (2,94%) Caiado – 668.442 (2,37%) Diferentemente do que diz o influenciador, Flávio não acumulou mais de 2 milhões de votos entre uma parcial e outra, mas 1,4 milhão de votos adicionais, contra 1,2 milhão acrescentados a Lula no mesmo intervalo. O percentual de cada candidato é recalculado com base no total de votos apurados em cada atualização, incluindo também os votos destinados aos outros concorrentes. Para manter ou ampliar os 51,07% das 18h23min, Flávio precisaria ter obtido uma proporção de votos superior a esse índice nas urnas adicionadas à apuração. Mas, como sua participação entre o novo total de votos foi menor, seu percentual recuou 0,13 ponto, para 50,94%, mesmo com o aumento do número absoluto. A Reuters entrou em contato com o influenciador que publicou o vídeo, mas não teve retorno até a publicação deste texto. VEREDICTO Enganoso. O percentual de Flávio Bolsonaro caiu porque a proporção de votos para ele dentro do total diminuiu entre as parciais mostradas no vídeo. Este artigo foi produzido pela equipe da Reuters Fact Check. item.title: US court warns more Jackson Walker cases could be tainted by relationship with judge
item.description: US law firm Jackson Walker is facing potential sanctions for not disclosing its work on ATM maker Diebold Nixdorf's 2023 bankruptcy, deepening the firm's potential fallout from a prior relationship between one of its lawyers and a Houston bankruptcy judge.
item.dc:creator: David Thomas
item.content:encoded: US law firm Jackson Walker is facing potential sanctions for not disclosing its work on ATM maker Diebold Nixdorf's 2023 bankruptcy, deepening the firm's potential fallout from a prior relationship between one of its lawyers and a Houston bankruptcy judge. Chief US Bankruptcy Judge Eduardo Rodriguez in Houston ordered Jackson Walker on Friday to explain why it should not be sanctioned for failing to disclose its work in the Diebold case to the court or other authorities scrutinizing its fees in cases involving former US Bankruptcy Judge David Jones. Jones presided over Diebold's Chapter 11 case before he [USN:L4N3BL0B7 TEXT:"resigned"] in October 2023, after admitting he was romantically involved with a Jackson Walker partner. "Most troubling to the court is the unanswered question of how many other cases like this may be lurking on the dockets of the Southern District of Texas bankruptcy courts," Rodriguez said. Rodriguez said he was considering recommending the appointment of a special master to investigate other potentially undisclosed cases in which Jackson Walker appeared in cases before Jones. He ordered the law firm to submit a list of all such cases by October 15. A spokesperson for Jackson Walker declined to comment. The firm was co-counsel to Diebold in the Chapter 11 along with Jones Day. A spokesperson for Jones Day did not immediately respond to a request for comment. A Diebold spokesperson declined to comment. Jackson Walker is already mired in litigation over nearly three dozen past bankruptcy matters that Jones oversaw. The US Justice Department's bankruptcy watchdog, the Office of the US Trustee, is seeking to force the law firm to disgorge its fees in those cases. Jackson Walker [USN:L6N4400XF TEXT:"has been negotiating a $15 million settlement"] to end its fee dispute with the US Trustee, which is currently set for trial in January. The settlement is subject to court approval by US District Judge Alia Moses. A Justice Department spokesperson declined to comment but referred Reuters to its Friday status report in the case, in which the US Trustee said it faced "procedural impediments" in reaching a settlement with the law firm. Jones, based in Houston, once oversaw [USN:L1N3E92K8 TEXT:"the busiest bankruptcy docket in the country"]. Jackson Walker [USN:L1N3CE240 TEXT:"has said"] it was deceived into thinking its partner's relationship with Jones had ended in March 2020. The partner is no longer at the firm. Diebold, which sells ATMs and point-of-sale systems in more than 100 countries, filed for bankruptcy in June 2023, saying it had reached an agreement to reduce its overall debt by $2.1 billion. A hearing in the Diebold case is scheduled for October 22.
