item.description: US President Donald Trump is preparing an executive order to expand access to tax-exempt diesel that will be unveiled as soon as Monday, two sources familiar with the matter said.
item.dc:creator: Jarrett Renshaw
item.content:encoded: US President Donald Trump is preparing an executive order to expand access to tax-exempt diesel that will be unveiled as soon as Monday, two sources familiar with the matter said. High diesel prices, which shot to a record of about $6.50 a gallon last month, are a risk to Trump ahead of the Nov. 3 elections. Prices for the fuel integral to trucking goods have risen in response to the wars in Iran and Ukraine which have led to attacks on refineries in Russia and the Middle East. The order is expected to contain a variety of ways to expand access to diesel which could include making more available so-called red dye diesel fuel which is used by the agriculture industry and by some off-road vehicles, the sources said. A third source said the order will likely direct the US Department of Transportation to coordinate with states to waive taxes on road diesel. G7 countries announced last week that they would release 100 million barrels of diesel, after pressure from Trump who had considered banning US exports of the fuel. But it was not clear how much of that release would be entirely new supplies or compliance with a global agreement in March. Bloomberg first reported the news on the executive order.

item.title: Liverpool match looms but Man City will know what to expect at Anfield
item.description: Manchester City face a hostile reception at Liverpool on Sunday in their first game since being found guilty of serious breaches of the Premier League's financial rules, though how much the verdict will affect the leaders remains unclear.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Manchester City face a hostile reception at Liverpool on Sunday in their first game since being found guilty of serious breaches of the Premier League's financial rules, though how much the verdict will affect the leaders remains unclear. Fan chatrooms have been humming with opinion and invective but that is nothing new when it comes to relations between the old rivals. The "[USN:L6N45L10S TEXT:"sham" commercial contract case"] has hung over the Premier League for years and may rumble on for some time yet after City filed an appeal. Just how much it spills over into the stands at Anfield, and grounds beyond that over the course of the season, remains to be seen. "If they want an understanding of how angry the game is going to be, then Anfield will tell them like you would never believe," former Manchester United captain and England defender Gary Neville declared recently on The Overlap podcast. "I suspect there may be banners, there will certainly be chanting. There will be a reception like you have never seen for them at Anfield...it will be a brutal day." Merseyside Police said there would be an appropriate policing operation in place on the day. CITY CHARGED Other commentators said that Liverpool supporters had been calling City cheats since they were charged by the Premier League [USN:L4N3P11BV TEXT:"in February 2023."] "Man City players already know what rival fans will do amid charges fallout," read a headline in the Manchester Evening news on Monday. "City players won't necessarily be walking into anything new when they resume their club duties this weekend," wrote the paper's chief City reporter. "It is not going to be pretty, but it will be a surprise if it catches the players off guard given how used to the abuse they are." City are unbeaten and three points clear of champions Arsenal at the top of the table, five ahead of third-placed Brighton & Hove Albion. They are likely to still be top by the time of Sunday's match even if Arsenal beat Leeds United on Saturday, given the four-goal difference between them. One contributor on the lfcreds.com website said the best response was for Liverpool to beat City on the field and the fans to make their feelings heard inside Anfield on the day. "Could this be one of the first games that pretty much everyone in the country wants us to win?," asked another.

item.title: US to announce $150 million for Alaska power lines as Vance campaigns in Senate battleground
item.description: The US Energy Department will announce $150 million in new funding for power lines in Alaska on Monday as Vice President JD Vance visits the state, where Republicans are fighting to hold a critical Senate seat in the November midterm elections.
item.dc:creator: Jacob Bogage
item.content:encoded: The US Energy Department will announce $150 million in new funding for power lines in Alaska on Monday as Vice President JD Vance visits the state, where Republicans are fighting to hold a critical Senate seat in the November midterm elections. Vance is set to rally voters for Republican Senator Dan Sullivan, who is locked in a tight reelection battle with Democrat Mary Peltola. Flipping the seat is key to the Democratic Party's strategy to take control of the US Senate, and recent polls have Peltola, a former member of the US House of Representatives, leading Sullivan. The energy plan is the latest in a series of economic and investment announcements President Donald Trump and his administration have highlighted ahead of the midterms amid voter concerns over the Iran war and high gasoline prices. Under the Energy Department plan, the Trump administration will tap federal funds to help construct 223 miles (359 km) of new electrical transmission lines linking the Beluga power station on Alaska's southern coast with Healy in the state's interior, an administration official told Reuters. The corridor between Beluga and Healy covers major ports and nearly three-quarters of the state's roughly 735,000-person population. The total cost of the project is $400 million, the official said. SOUTH KOREA BACKED ALASKA PIPELINE CONDITIONALLY A New York Times poll that concluded October 1 placed Peltola ahead by 7 percentage points. Other polls indicate the race is about even. Alaska, with its far-flung and rural population, is often difficult for pollsters to gauge. Trump [USN:L1N45M0IK TEXT:"unveiled plans"] last week for South Korea to invest some $200 billion in US projects, including for an Alaska liquefied natural gas pipeline. But Seoul quickly said the pipeline would only proceed if certain commercial and legal conditions were met. Both Sullivan and Peltola have made affordability — and energy — primary issues in their campaigns. Sullivan supports drilling for oil and gas in Alaska's protected wilderness and has called on Trump to ban diesel exports amid the economic fallout from conflict with Iran and the Russian war in Ukraine. Peltola has called for refining more oil and natural gas in Alaska but does not support drilling for resources in the environmentally fragile wilderness. She has also advocated for federal tax credits for solar, wind and hydropower projects.

item.title: US commodities regulator proposes new federal crypto oversight rules
item.description: The US commodities regulator proposed on Monday a new federal framework for cryptocurrency exchanges that offer leveraged digital asset trading, seeking to bring parts of the spot crypto market under federal oversight weeks after Congress failed to advance comprehensive crypto regulation.
item.dc:creator: Hannah Lang
item.content:encoded: The US commodities regulator proposed on Monday a new federal framework for cryptocurrency exchanges that offer leveraged digital asset trading, seeking to bring parts of the spot crypto market under federal oversight weeks after Congress failed to advance comprehensive crypto regulation. The US Commodity Futures Trading Commission's proposed rules would effectively allow US crypto exchanges to opt into a federal regulatory framework instead of relying primarily on a patchwork of state money-transmitter licenses, the agency said. The proposed rules make use of a specific authority the CFTC has to oversee margined or leveraged spot assets. The CFTC has long sought authority to regulate spot cryptocurrency markets — which currently operate in a regulatory grey area — but only Congress has the ability to provide the regulator with that purview. "For years, entrepreneurs building on the new frontier of finance faced uncertainty about whether there was a place for them in our markets. We are giving them an answer," said CFTC Chairman Michael Selig in a speech on Monday at an event in New York held by Fordham University's law school. RULES WOULD ESTABLISH NEW TRADING VENUE CATEGORY Under the proposed rules, the CFTC would establish a new category of CFTC-regulated trading venues called a "crypto asset market" for exchanges that offer leveraged or margined trading to retail customers. Those platforms would be subject to specific requirements including anti-market-manipulation controls and a "proof of reserves" obligation. The CFTC is also proposing that registered futures commission merchants intermediate customer trades on the new category of exchanges. The agency is not stipulating specific leverage limits, but any exchange offering a leveraged transaction would have to clear that product with CFTC staff, the agency said. The proposed rules come after Congress [USN:L1N4560M2 TEXT:"failed to advance"] a major crypto bill, called the Clarity Act, which would have created new rules for the $2 trillion cryptocurrency market, putting the industry on a firmer legal footing. One of the key components of the bill was the explicit authority for the CFTC to police the spot crypto market. The impasse in Congress has put the onus on US President Donald Trump's crypto-friendly regulators, particularly the Securities and Exchange Commission and the CFTC, to give the industry [USN:L1N39023I TEXT:"the regulatory clarity"] it has long argued it lacks. Still, [USN:L1N4490UR TEXT:"analysts have said"] that without legislation, regulations could be vulnerable to the shifting political climate and court challenges, creating lingering hazards for the crypto industry.

item.title: Nasdaq cierra en récord, inversores se centran en los resultados corporativos
item.description: El Nasdaq cerró en un récord histórico el lunes, impulsado por Nvidia y Microsoft, mientras los inversores se centraron en la caída de los precios del petróleo y esperaban con interés los informes de resultados trimestrales.
item.dc:creator: Tharuniyaa Lakshmi, Shashwat Chauhan
item.content:encoded: El Nasdaq cerró en un récord histórico el lunes, impulsado por Nvidia y Microsoft, mientras los inversores se centraron en la caída de los precios del petróleo y esperaban con interés los informes de resultados trimestrales. * La jornada del lunes fue la segunda seguida de fuertes avances para el Nasdaq, después de que los datos de empleo del viernes, peores de lo esperado, frenaran las expectativas de un alza de las tasas de interés por parte de la Reserva Federal este mes. * "Dado que la agenda de datos económicos es escasa y que aún queda una semana para la publicación de resultados, los inversores están buscando a ciegas cualquier aspecto positivo al que aferrarse, y está claro que están fijándose en la baja de los precios de la energía", afirmó Art Hogan, estratega jefe de mercados de B. Riley Wealth. * La temporada de resultados del tercer trimestre arranca la próxima semana con los informes de los grandes bancos. Según datos de LSEG, los analistas prevén, de media, que los beneficios del S&P 500 aumenten más de un 30% interanual. * Según los datos preliminares de cierre, el S&P 500 (.SPX) subió 51,50 puntos, o un 0,67%, a 7.774,22 puntos; mientras que el Nasdaq Composite (.IXIC) subió 289,42 puntos, o un 1,06%, a 27.480,28 unidades. El Dow Jones (.DJI) subió 94,59 puntos, o un 0,18%, a 51. 274,32. * El anterior máximo histórico de cierre del Nasdaq se registró el 22 de septiembre. * El optimismo sobre los sólidos resultados empresariales ha contribuido a que las acciones estadounidenses hayan superado a sus rivales globales en los últimos seis meses, a pesar del inestable panorama geopolítico y de las preocupaciones por la inflación. * Los analistas de Goldman Sachs prevén que la mayoría de las empresas "volverán a superar las estimaciones de beneficios consensuadas este trimestre", y señalan un crecimiento interanual de los beneficios del 9% para la mediana de las acciones del S&P 500. * Los operadores estiman ahora que hay un 80% de probabilidades de que la Reserva Federal mantenga las tasas de interés sin cambios este mes, aunque, según la herramienta FedWatch de la CME, el mercado sigue descontando en gran medida una subida de tasas en diciembre.

item.title: Bolsas y monedas suben; Brasil brilla por expectativas de cambio de Gobierno
item.description: La monedas y las bolsas latinoamericanas se fortalecieron el lunes, en especial el real brasileño, que ganó más de un 4% y rompió la barrera de las 5 unidades por dólar, tras la sorpresiva ventaja del candidato de extrema derecha Flávio Bolsonaro en la primera vuelta de las elecciones presidenciales.
item.dc:creator: Javier Lérida
item.content:encoded: La monedas y las bolsas latinoamericanas se fortalecieron el lunes, en especial el real brasileño, que ganó más de un 4% y rompió la barrera de las 5 unidades por dólar, tras la sorpresiva ventaja del candidato de extrema derecha Flávio Bolsonaro en la primera vuelta de las elecciones presidenciales. Las monedas, desde el peso mexicano al chileno, subieron pese al alza del dólar en los mercados internacionales y un avance de los rendimientos de largo plazo en Estados Unidos. La mayor parte del avance regional provenía de Brasil, por las expectativas de que Bolsonaro gane la segunda vuelta y adopte políticas más favorables al mercado a partir de enero. El real se fortalecía cerca del cierre un 4,14%, a 4,9975 reales por dólar, mientras que el índice de referencia de la bolsa, el Bovespa (.BVSP) , se empinaba un 8,8%, a 209.075 puntos. El peso mexicano también avanzó, por segunda sesión consecutiva, debido a las menores expectativas de que la Reserva Federal suba su tasa de interés este mes. La moneda mexicana cerró en 18,0899 unidades por dólar, con una ganancia del 0,30% frente al precio de referencia de LSEG del viernes, cuando avanzó un 0,72%. El índice líder S&P/BMV IPC (.MXX) que agrupa a las acciones más negociadas del mercado local, subía un 0,62%, a 64.933,43 puntos. El peso colombiano se apreció, por segunda sesión consecutiva, un 1,98%, a 3.200 unidades por dólar, mientras que el índice accionario de la bolsa, el MSCI COLCAP (.COLCAP) se valorizó un 2,69%, a 2.532,69 puntos. El peso chileno , subió un 1,89%, a 973,80/974,10 unidades por dólar, impulsado a un máximo de una semana por una licitación de dólares del Gobierno. En tanto, el principal índice de la bolsa de comercio de Santiago, el IPSA (.SPIPSA) avanzó un 1,9%, con 11.123,80 puntos. La bolsa argentina se recuperaba de un retroceso de más de un 4% de la semana pasada y de un 7% en septiembre, con un alza del índice Merval de un 3,8%. En tanto, el peso argentino interbancario se apreció un 0,07%, a 1.520,5 unidades por dólar para la venta. "Consideramos que el resultado electoral (...) en Brasil es favorable para Argentina. La ventaja de dos puntos de Bolsonaro lo deja al borde de una victoria, y creemos que un real más fuerte, tasas más bajas y la presencia de un aliado natural dentro del Mercosur juegan a favor de los planes del presidente (argentino Javier) Milei", dijo la consultora Max Capital. La moneda peruana, el sol , cerró estable en 3,4320/3,4360 unidades por dólar. En tanto que la Bolsa de Lima (.MXNUAMPESCPGPE) avanzó un 0,5%, a 1.583,31 puntos.

item.title: Plaza financiera argentina recupera fortaleza por resultado electoral en el vecino Brasil
item.description: La plaza financiera de Argentina operó con un alza generalizada el lunes en línea con la victoria electoral de la derecha en Brasil, un factor que ayuda a movilizar liquidez.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La plaza financiera de Argentina operó con un alza generalizada el lunes en línea con la victoria electoral de la derecha en Brasil, un factor que ayuda a movilizar liquidez. El optimismo inversor se adueñó de toda la región sudamericana, impactando de lleno en el riesgo país argentino que se retrotrajo por debajo de la línea de los 600 puntos. La mejora de precios se anotó tras importantes caídas recientes en el mercado doméstico, apoyada por una demanda liderada en papeles del sector financiero y en bonos atados a dólares. Brasil, principal socio comercial de Argentina, celebró [USN:L1N45R01Q TEXT:"comicios presidenciales el domingo"], donde se definió que el senador Flávio Bolsonaro se enfrentará a Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva en el balotaje que se llevará a cabo el 25 de octubre. La mayoría de las encuestas preveían este panorama, pero con Lula ganador en la primera ronda. El índice líder S&P Merval (.MERV) de la bolsa de Buenos Aires subió un 3,68% al cierre, donde se destacaron las mejoras de los papeles de los bancos BBVA (BBARm.BA) y Macro (BMAm.BA) con un 5,63% y 5,24%, respectivamente. Este mercado en particular viene de retroceder un 4,36% la semana previa y de finalizar septiembre con una pronunciada merma de 7,07%. "Consideramos que el resultado electoral de ayer (domingo) en Brasil es favorable para Argentina. La ventaja de dos puntos de Bolsonaro lo deja al borde de una victoria, y creemos que un real más fuerte, tasas más bajas y la presencia de un aliado natural dentro del Mercosur juegan a favor de los planes del presidente (argentino Javier) Milei", afirmó la consultora Max Capital. En tanto, el peso argentino interbancario se apreció muy leve 0,07% a 1.520,5 unidades por dólar para la venta, con la atenta mirada del banco central (BCRA), entidad que absorbió 14 millones de dólares de la plaza cambiaria única. La entidad monetaria, que busca reforzar sus reservas internacionales, adquirió 369 millones de dólares la semana previa y quedó cerca de alcanzar los 15.000 millones de dólares de compras en lo que va del año. Recientemente el secretario del Tesoro estadounidense, Scott Bessent, dejo abierta la posibilidad de volver a ayudar financieramente a Argentina. Bessent "afirmó que Estados Unidos podría repetir la asistencia financiera brindada a Argentina el año pasado. Consultado por Axios en una entrevista sobre la posibilidad de nuevas intervenciones en los mercados financieros, Bessent citó el caso de Argentina y señaló que Estados Unidos podría volver a hacerlo", agregó Max Capital. En octubre de 2025, el Tesoro estadounidense realizó compras de moneda argentina y alcanzó un [USN:L2N3VQ0V6 TEXT:"acuerdo"] para un intercambio de divisas por 20.000 millones de dólares con el BCRA. Los bonos del país austral en el segmento extrabursátil ganaron un 0,9% promedio, mientras que el riesgo país de Argentina se desplomaba a 599 puntos básicos (2130 GMT), luego de alcanzar las 655 unidades el viernes, su máximo nivel en 10 meses. "La suba del riesgo país junto con el mal contexto externo agregan presión al programa financiero 2027. Ahora, para conseguir los 5.000 millones de dólares previstos de emisiones locales, la tasa a convalidar es más del 11% (anual), algo que hasta hace poco era considerado caro", expresó Roberto Geretto, analista de Adcap Grupo Financiero. Por este contexto, los inversores financieras en Argentina muestran una notoria prudencia operativa.

item.title: US advances first government-funded trials of psychedelic drug ibogaine
item.description: US health officials are advancing the first government-funded clinical trials of the psychedelic drug ibogaine to treat opioid addiction and post-traumatic stress disorder, the FDA said on Monday, as it sought public feedback on safety rules for the studies.
item.dc:creator: Kamal Choudhury
item.content:encoded: US health officials are advancing the first government-funded clinical trials of the psychedelic drug ibogaine to treat opioid addiction and post-traumatic stress disorder, the FDA said on Monday, as it sought public feedback on safety rules for the studies. The initiative follows an April executive order by President Donald Trump, dedicating [USN:L6N41103Y TEXT:"$50 million"] to the federal ibogaine research, as well as [USN:L1N4560R3 TEXT:"recent calls"] by experts and veterans for strict safety standards on psychedelic treatments. The Food and Drug Administration said it has opened a public docket seeking feedback on trial design, dose selection, patient eligibility, safety monitoring, study-stopping rules and oversight by November 20. "This is the most important regulatory signal ibogaine has received in decades," said Tom Feegel, CEO of Beond, a Mexico-based ibogaine treatment provider. The Department of Health and Human Services is funding early-stage trials of ibogaine through the Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health and the National Institute on Drug Abuse, a federal notice showed. The FDA has previously warned that the drug carries severe health risks, including life-threatening irregular heart rhythms and potential brain toxicity. Ibogaine, a compound found in the roots of the [USN:L1N4570B8 TEXT:"African shrub iboga"], is classified as an illegal Schedule I controlled substance under US law. "Cardiac safety is not a footnote ... it is the central challenge researchers have to solve before this treatment can responsibly reach the people who need it," said Betty Aldworth, co-executive director of the Multidisciplinary Association for Psychedelic Studies.

item.title: What to know about Spain's November snap election
item.description: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez has called an early election for November 29 that he hopes will hand him a parliamentary majority but which could just as easily usher in a conservative coalition, as the centre-left bloc trails in most opinion polls.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez has [USN:L8N45R05N TEXT:"called an early election"] for November 29 that he hopes will hand him a parliamentary majority but which could just as easily usher in a conservative coalition, as the centre-left bloc trails in most opinion polls. Here is what you need to know about the election: POLLS PITCH RIGHT-WING COALITION AS LIKELIEST OUTCOME Sanchez's Socialist Party (PSOE) has long trailed in the polls, hovering around 28% and never above 33% throughout his eight years in office. Parties further to the left, which will be key for Sanchez to cobble together a coalition, are currently polling at around 8%. A coalition between the conservative People's Party (PP) and far-right Vox is the only combination projected to win enough votes for an absolute majority in the 350-seat lower house of parliament. Voting intention for Vox stands at roughly 18%, propelled by younger and male voters. ISSUES LIKELY TO DOMINATE THE ELECTORAL CAMPAIGN Housing will dominate the left's agenda, with Sanchez taking the decision to call the election after protests erupted across the country following the high-profile eviction of an 87-year-old woman from her Madrid home. Immigration is likely to be another defining issue, both for Sanchez as one of Europe's loudest advocates of immigration's benefits for society and the economy, recently [USN:L8N42N0Y2 TEXT:"granting legal status"] to nearly a million undocumented migrants, and for Vox, which wants far tighter controls. The mass crossing of 72,000 migrants [USN:L8N43W1SU TEXT:"into Ceuta in July"] has overwhelmed local authorities and triggered major political disputes over Spain's ability to control its borders. Corruption: Opposition parties are expected to make corruption a central theme of the election campaign, seeking to tie Sanchez to a series of investigations, trials and convictions involving members of his [USN:L8N42U0LE TEXT:"inner circle"] and [USN:L1N42S02V TEXT:"family"]. Sanchez has repeatedly denied any wrongdoing and argued that some of the cases form part of a [USN:L1N4260JB TEXT:"politically motivated campaign"] against his government. CANDIDATES FOR PRIME MINISTER Sanchez, the incumbent, will run again for the Socialists, having spearheaded the party since 2017. Now seeking a third term after eight years in office, he is already Spain's second-longest-serving premier since the country returned to democracy in 1978. Despite a tenure dogged in the past two years by [USN:L1N42U0KB TEXT:"corruption investigations"], the Socialist leader is betting that the housing crisis and the prospect of a far-right party coming to power will help mobilise left-leaning voters who might have otherwise abstained. Alberto Nuñez Feijoo, former president of the region of Galicia, will run against Sanchez representing the People's Party, which he has led since April 2022. A four-time winner of presidential elections in Galicia, Feijoo built a reputation in his years governing the region as a moderate and pragmatic administrator. The PP emerged as the largest party in the 2023 general election but failed to secure enough support to form a government, leaving Feijoo as leader of the opposition. Since then, Feijoo has sought to position the PP as a government-in-waiting, piling criticism on Sanchez for everything from his policies to the corruption allegations encircling his party. A CABINET ROLE FOR THE FAR RIGHT? Polls project that the PP would rely on far-right Vox to govern, giving a far-right party a role in cabinet for the first time since the death of former dictator Francisco Franco in 1975. Its leader is Santiago Abascal, who built his political profile in the Basque Country opposing separatism and co-founded the party in 2014 alongside others defecting from or seeking an alternative to the PP. Under Abascal, Vox has evolved from a minor political force into the country's third-largest party. It advocates tougher immigration controls, recentralisation of state powers, lower taxes and the reversal of many progressive social policies. A MOBILISED LEFT? THE 'BROAD FRONT' A swathe of parties to the left of PSOE are planning to launch a new common platform called "Broad Front" (Frente Amplio), which will be Sanchez's best hope of maintaining power if it supports the Socialists in coalition as previously. The alliance would replace Sumar, a hard-left platform founded in 2023 by Labour Minister Yolanda Diaz which acted as coalition partner to Sanchez's government in his final term. The new front will name a leadership candidate at a launch event on October 17, after Diaz said she would not stand as leader again. Podemos, former junior coalition partners to PSOE who take a more critical line than Sumar, has for now refused to join the front, opting to run separately unless open primaries are held. OTHER PARTIES Spain's parliament is highly fragmented, giving minor parties that hold just a handful of seats the power to tip the scales on passing policy. The country's historically distinct regions feature four separatist parties: EH Bildu in the Basque Country, BNG in Galicia, and two in Catalonia — the left-leaning ERC and the right-leaning Junts. While EH Bildu, BNG and ERC have broadly supported Sanchez, Junts has frequently vetoed his government's measures, including the housing decrees that prompted the prime minister to dissolve parliament.

item.title: Right-wing wave in Brazil's Congress boosts Bolsonaro camp ahead of presidential runoff
item.description: Brazil's right-wing Liberal Party, home to Senator Flavio Bolsonaro's presidential bid, emerged as the biggest winner in congressional elections on Sunday, securing the largest single-party representation in both the Senate and the lower house.
item.dc:creator: Fernando Cardoso, Ricardo Brito, Lisandra Paraguassu
item.content:encoded: Brazil's right-wing Liberal Party, home to Senator Flavio Bolsonaro's presidential bid, emerged as the biggest winner in congressional elections on Sunday, securing the largest single-party representation in both the Senate and the lower house. Senator Bolsonaro, the eldest son of former President Jair Bolsonaro, on Sunday [USN:L6N45Q04L TEXT:"won the most votes"] in the first round of the presidential race, advancing to a runoff against leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva on October 25. During the campaign, the younger Bolsonaro stumped often for allied Senate candidates. His Liberal Party (PL) increased its representation in the Senate from 15 to 28 seats, the strongest result for a party since Brazil's constitution was enacted in the late 1980s, following the country's return to democracy. It also secured 121 seats in the lower house, projections for that chamber showed, up from 98 seats currently. Combined with other center-to-right parties and blocs, which were projected to win close to 250 seats in the lower house and more than 30 seats in the Senate, the Bolsonaro agenda looks set to enjoy a healthy working majority in the next Congress. An allied Congress — and particularly Senate — would help the younger Bolsonaro achieve his aim of granting amnesty to his father, who is serving a 27-year sentence for plotting a coup after losing the 2022 election. The Senate's pro-Bolsonaro bloc may even be close to the threshold of 54 votes needed to impeach the Supreme Court justices who convicted the far-right former leader. "I was very happy to see how many Brazilians went to the polls to make their voices heard and didn't stay on the sidelines because they want change," Bolsonaro said after the vote. Sunday's legislative races, held alongside the [USN:L6N45Q04L TEXT:"first round"] of the presidential election, renewed all 513 seats in the lower house of Congress and two-thirds of the 81-seat Senate. Congressional races in Brazil have drawn increasing voter attention in recent elections as lawmakers expand their influence in the capital Brasilia, particularly through greater control over federal spending and leverage over [USN:L1N45K0U9 TEXT:"presidential appointments"]. Lula's Workers Party, known as PT, also increased its footprint in Congress. The party maintained its Senate presence with nine seats, and a three-party bloc led by the PT was projected to win 88 seats in the lower house, up from 82 currently. GOVERNANCE CHALLENGES Even as Lula fights for a come-from-behind victory in the second round of voting, analysts say the next Congress would make his fourth, non-consecutive term an uphill battle. "Governance would pose a major challenge for President Lula," said Neuriberg Dias, head of legislative watchdog DIAP, adding that a right-wing bloc would work to stifle legislative progress and the functioning of government. Both political camps have illustrated the difficulties faced by presidents who do not have sufficient congressional backing. In April, Lula became the first Brazilian president in more than a century to see a Supreme Court nominee [USN:L1N41C1VC TEXT:"voted down"] amid tensions with center-right Senate President Davi Alcolumbre. Congress has also overturned dozens of Lula's vetoes since his return to office in January 2023, underscoring lawmakers' growing assertiveness. Former President Jair Bolsonaro faced similar obstacles, with Congress blocking some of his most prominent policy initiatives, including efforts to loosen gun-control rules and introduce a printed ballot verification system for elections.

item.title: Açúcar bruto atinge maior cotação em 19 meses; café também sobe
item.description: Os contratos futuros de açúcar bruto na bolsa ICE subiram 4% nesta segunda-feira, ultrapassando os 20 centavos por libra-peso e atingindo a maior cotação em 19 meses, à medida que aumentavam as preocupações com novas chuvas excessivas relacionadas ao El Niño no Brasil, principal produtor.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Os contratos futuros de açúcar bruto na bolsa ICE subiram 4% nesta segunda-feira, ultrapassando os 20 centavos por libra-peso e atingindo a maior cotação em 19 meses, à medida que aumentavam as preocupações com novas chuvas excessivas relacionadas ao El Niño no Brasil, principal produtor. AÇÚCAR * O primeiro contrato fechou com alta de 0,8 centavo, ou 4%, a 20,73 centavos por libra-peso, após atingir a máxima de 19 meses de 20,81 centavos. O contrato registrou alta de 7,7% na semana passada. * "Dadas as chuvas recordes em setembro... e a perspectiva de mais chuvas ao longo de outubro, parece que o mercado está convencido de que a produção de açúcar ficará bem abaixo das estimativas", afirmaram analistas da Green Pool. * A produção brasileira caiu 41,6% na primeira quinzena de setembro devido ao excesso de chuvas. Também há alguns atrasos no carregamento de açúcar nos portos brasileiros devido às condições climáticas, segundo corretores. * Espera-se que o El Niño afete negativamente as safras nos três principais produtores de açúcar -- Brasil, Índia e Tailândia. A próxima safra da União Europeia também deve cair drasticamente devido à seca deste verão. * O contrato de açúcar branco subiu 3%, para US$547,60 por tonelada métrica, após atingir a maior cotação desde o final de agosto, em US$ 552,50. CAFÉ * O café arábica fechou com alta de 3,8 centavos, ou 1,3%, a US$2,9255 por libra-peso, após ter subido 3,6% na semana passada. * O café arábica tem sido impulsionado no curto prazo por preocupações com a qualidade, devido ao excesso de chuvas associadas ao El Niño no Brasil, principal produtor, e pelo temor de que o padrão climático possa causar seca no futuro. * David Behrends, da Sucafina, disse que, embora ainda se espere uma safra abundante no Brasil em 2026/27, alguns participantes do mercado permanecem "altistas" no curto prazo devido aos estoques reduzidos e aos preços físicos elevados na Colômbia e na América Central. * Os corretores observaram um salto de quase 5% na moeda brasileira, o real, na segunda-feira, após os resultados das eleições aumentarem as chances do candidato presidencial de direita Flávio Bolsonaro. Uma moeda local mais forte geralmente desacelera as vendas dos produtores. * O preço do café robusta subiu 1,7%, para US$3.528 por tonelada. * O Vietnã, maior produtor de robusta, exportou 1,45 milhão de toneladas métricas de café nos primeiros nove meses de 2026, um aumento de 16,2%. CACAU * O cacau em Londres fechou com alta de £143 , ou 3,4%, a £4.382 por tonelada. * Os corretores afirmaram que o cacau permanece, em geral, dentro de uma faixa estreita, preso entre o excesso de oferta atual e uma perspectiva cada vez mais desfavorável para a safra 2026/27, associada ao El Niño. * A safra principal da Costa do Marfim deve cair cerca de 17% nesta temporada, de acordo com uma pesquisa da Reuters, enquanto os agricultores marfinenses afirmaram nesta segunda-feira que a escassez de chuvas amplia o risco de encurtar a safra principal, que vai de setembro a fevereiro. * As chegadas de cacau aos portos da Costa do Marfim totalizaram 18.000 toneladas métricas na semana encerrada em 4 de outubro, elevando o total desde o início da safra 2025/26 para 54.500 toneladas. * O contrato de futuros de cacau de Nova York subiu 3,5%, para US$5.867 por tonelada. (Por May Angel e Marcelo Teixeira)

item.title: Nigerian military aircraft crashes, killing 32
item.description: A Nigerian military plane flying from Benin City to Lagos crashed on Monday in southwestern Ondo state, killing 25 passengers and seven crew members.
item.dc:creator: Camillus Eboh, Macdonald Dzirutwe
item.content:encoded: A Nigerian military plane flying from Benin City to Lagos crashed on Monday in southwestern Ondo state, killing 25 passengers and seven crew members. President Bola Tinubu, confirming that there were no survivors, expressed "profound sadness" and extended condolences to the families of those aboard. "The Chief of Air Staff has briefed me, and I have directed the Nigerian Air Force to immediately commence a thorough investigation into the cause of the crash to prevent future occurrences," Tinubu said in a statement. The Air Force ATR-42 aircraft was on a routine mission from Benin City to Lagos when air traffic controllers lost contact with it at 0813 GMT on Monday, Aviation Minister Festus Keyamo said. The accident was one of the deadliest air disasters in Nigeria in recent years. The wreckage was later located near the coastal town of Igbokoda, where search and rescue teams were deployed.

item.title: Democratic lawmakers urge FAA not to drop rule requiring epinephrine on all flights
item.description: A group of Democratic lawmakers urged the Federal Aviation Administration on Monday not to relax a requirement that all US airlines keep epinephrine on board flights for medical emergencies, especially severe allergic reactions.
item.dc:creator: David Shepardson
item.content:encoded: A group of Democratic lawmakers urged the Federal Aviation Administration on Monday not to relax a requirement that all US airlines keep epinephrine on board flights for medical emergencies, especially severe allergic reactions. "Having multiple doses of epinephrine on every aircraft, in delivery methods that can be easily self-administered by individuals without medical training, is more urgent than ever," said the letter sent by Senators Tammy Duckworth, Chuck Schumer, Cory Booker, Richard Blumenthal and Tammy Baldwin, as well as Representative Doris Matsui and more than a dozen other lawmakers. The lawmakers said it was crucial given "the on-flight presence of food items containing unlabeled allergens, a steady increase in the number of children with food allergies, the increased prevalence of a tick-borne illness that could create life-threatening allergies and the very real possibility that more than one passenger may require epinephrine during a single flight." The FAA in August proposed giving airlines flexibility in requirements for emergency medical kits on flights, dropping a checklist of medical items and setting performance-based standards requiring carriers to have sufficient resources to manage nine life-threatening conditions. The FAA declined to comment but said it will "consider all applicable comments" before finalizing new regulations. The lawmakers noted an FAA working group in 2025 recommended a "pre-measured auto-delivery device" for epinephrine be required in contrast with the agency's proposed action. The letter said JetBlue Airways (JBLU.O) , Southwest (LUV.N) , Frontier (ULCC.O) and Breeze Airways stock their kits with epinephrine auto-injectors, and American Airlines’ (AAL.O) includes both adult- and pediatric-dose epinephrine auto-injectors. Delta Air Lines (DAL.N) is transitioning its fleet to include auto-injectors in their kits by September 2027 and United Airlines (UAL.O) and Allegiant Air (ALGT.O) will begin this year the work to include auto-injectors in kits. The American Medical Association has also raised concerns, telling the FAA that "allowing individual airlines to determine their own medical supplies could compromise passenger safety during in-flight emergencies," citing concerns about epinephrine and some diagnostic tools.

item.title: US Supreme Court rejects Nexstar bid to avoid DirecTV lawsuit over fees
item.description: The US Supreme Court declined on Monday to hear a bid by Nexstar Media Group , which owns numerous local television stations, to block an antitrust suit by DirecTV challenging allegedly inflated content-distribution fees.
item.dc:creator: Mike Scarcella
item.content:encoded: The US Supreme Court declined on Monday to hear a bid by Nexstar Media Group (NXST.O) , which owns numerous local television stations, to block an antitrust suit by DirecTV challenging allegedly inflated content-distribution fees. The justices turned away Nexstar's appeal of a lower court's decision to reinstate streaming and satellite TV provider DirecTV's lawsuit in federal court in New York City. DirecTV alleged in its 2023 lawsuit that Nexstar and two station owners violated antitrust law by depriving it of a competitive process for rights to rebroadcast certain channels in specific markets. DirecTV accused the three companies of secretly working together to demand artificially high fees, in violation of antitrust law. DirecTV refused to pay the prices, and some stations went dark for a million DirecTV subscribers. DirecTV says thousands of customers canceled their subscriptions as a result, and the company lost revenue. Irving, Texas-headquartered Nexstar has argued that a company can sue over price-fixing only if it actually pays allegedly inflated prices. El Segundo, California-headquartered DirecTV, according to Nexstar, has no right to sue. According to its website, Nexstar and its subsidiaries and partners own or operate 265 stations in 132 markets in 44 US states. A federal judge dismissed DirecTV's lawsuit. But the New York-based 2nd US Circuit Court of Appeals [USN:L6N3XN0A7 TEXT:"ruled"] in December that DirecTV could pursue its antitrust claims based on its allegations of lost profits when it was unable to distribute those channels. Nexstar told the Supreme Court in a filing that the 2nd Circuit's ruling conflicts with decisions by other federal appeals courts. DirecTV disputed that any conflict exists. The 2nd Circuit order, Nexstar also said, "has exposed sellers to sweeping liability" and could threaten to subject defendants to "coercive settlement pressure divorced from any concrete market injury."

item.title: US Supreme Court won't hear Zillow's bid to escape investor class action
item.description: The US Supreme Court declined on Monday to hear a bid by real estate platform Zillow Group to escape a class action that accused it of misleading investors about its failed home-flipping venture.
item.dc:creator: Jan Wolfe
item.content:encoded: The US Supreme Court declined on Monday to hear a bid by real estate platform Zillow Group (ZG.O) to escape a class action that accused it of misleading investors about its failed home-flipping venture. The court turned away Seattle-based Zillow's appeal of a lower court's decision that allowed the 2021 lawsuit to move forward in federal court in Washington state. "We look forward to now moving this case to trial," said Steve Berman, a lawyer at the Hagens Berman law firm which brought the class action. Zillow did not respond to a request for comment. At issue in the case is what defenses publicly traded companies can raise in lawsuits alleging they made false statements to the investing public. In such class actions, which are common in US courts, plaintiffs' lawyers frequently allege that companies made misrepresentations designed not to actively drive up their stock price, but simply to keep it from falling. The Zillow dispute is an example of one of these cases, known as "price-maintenance" cases. Zillow's stock plunged in November 2021 because the company announced it was permanently shutting down Zillow Offers, its home-flipping division, after management admitted it could not accurately forecast future home prices. The company disclosed that it wrote down $300 million in losses during the previous quarter and announced a layoff of 25% of its workforce. Investors sued in federal court, saying statements made by Zillow's then-CEO and other company leaders in the preceding months painted an overly positive picture of the business unit. Zillow's lawyers denied that the company had engaged in securities fraud. "Zillow made a business decision to enter a new line of business, disclosing all of the risk in doing so, that in the end simply did not work out as the company had hoped," Zillow's lawyers said in a court filing. The San Francisco-based 9th US Circuit Court of Appeals last year upheld a judge's decision that allowed the case to move forward as a class action. The disclosures Zillow made in November 2021 "revealed new information about how Zillow's home-pricing struggles threatened the business and suggested that its earlier statements may have obscured how Zillow's pricing model misfired," the 9th Circuit said. In a filing asking the Supreme Court to hear its appeal, Zillow said the justices should clear up a split in federal appellate courts over how closely related a company's back-end corrective disclosures, which trigger a stock drop, must be to earlier alleged misstatements to justify certifying a class action. Pro-business lobbying groups including the US Chamber of Commerce have criticized the 9th Circuit decision, saying in a filing that this ruling deviated from Supreme Court precedent and "would expose American businesses to costly securities class-action lawsuits."

item.title: Les USA retirent leur bombardiers de la base britannique visée par un projet d'attaque présumé
item.description: Les États-Unis ont retiré leurs bombardiers B-1 de la base aérienne britannique de Fairford, dans l'ouest de la grande-Bretagne, qui aurait été la cible d'un projet d'attaque terroriste dans lequel Premier ministre britannique Andy Burnham n'a pas exclu la main de l'Iran.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Les États-Unis ont retiré leurs bombardiers B-1 de la base aérienne britannique de Fairford, dans l'ouest de la grande-Bretagne, qui aurait été la cible d'un [USN:L8N45J012 TEXT:"projet d'attaque"] terroriste dans lequel Premier ministre britannique Andy Burnham n'a pas exclu [USN:L8N45M1UT TEXT:"la main de l'Iran"]. Située à environ 145 kilomètres à l'ouest de Londres, la base de Fairford a été utilisée ces derniers mois par des bombardiers de l'armée américaine pour attaquer l'Iran. Le président américain Donald Trump a confirmé qu'une menace liée à l'Iran était à l'origine de cette décision. "Nous avions l'impression qu'il pourrait y avoir une menace, alors pourquoi est-ce que je les laisserais là ? Ca ne coûte que très peu d'argent de les déplacer", a déclaré le locataire de la Maison blanche à des journalistes. Le vice-président américain J.D. Vance avait lui aussi visé le régime iranien alors que le secrétaire d'Etat Marco Rubio avait écarté tout lien direct entre le retrait des bombardiers américains et la menace iranienne. Le Pentagone a précisé que tous les bombardiers déployés à Fairford avaient regagné leurs bases aux États-Unis, tout en affirmant que la flotte de bombardiers restait prête à mener des frappes de précision "partout et à tout moment". Cinq hommes âgés d'une vingtaine d'années et qui résident à Londres ont été interpellés il y a une semaine près de la base de Fairford, dans l'ouest du pays. [USN:L8N45K0XE TEXT:"Suspectés"] de préparer une attaque, ils ont été interrogés le lendemain par la police britannique puis libérés sous caution. L'Iran avait nié toute implication et son ministre des Affaires étrangères, Abbas Araqchi, avait qualifié les accusations de "sans fondement". Fin juillet, les Gardiens de la révolution iraniens avaient qualifié cette base de cible légitime. Une source militaire de l'Otan a déclaré lundi que l'Iran faisait toujours peser "une menace aiguë" pour les installations américaines au Royaume-Uni. Selon Christoph Bergs, analyste au Royal United Services Institute, le redéploiement des bombardiers réduira temporairement la capacité américaine à lancer rapidement des opérations contre l'Iran. Un haut responsable militaire de l'Otan a assuré que ce retrait des avions américains n'aurait pas d'impact sur l’Alliance. "La capacité défensive de l'Otan à faire face à toute agression reste inchangée et inégalée, grâce à l’unité, à la force et aux capacités combinées de 32 nations." Lundi, le ministère britannique de la Défense a refusé de commenter les mouvements des avions américains.

item.title: Yémen Les forces gouvernementales ont lancé une offensive sur Sanaa, progressent vers Bab el-Mandeb
item.description: Les forces armées gouvernementales yéménites ont annoncé lundi avoir lancé une "offensive stratégique" sur Sanaa, la capitale du Yémen, afin de reprendre le contrôle de la ville aux mains des rebelles houthis pro-iraniens.
item.dc:creator: Timour Azhari, Mohammed Ghobari
item.content:encoded: Les forces armées gouvernementales yéménites ont annoncé lundi avoir lancé une "offensive stratégique" sur Sanaa, la capitale du Yémen, afin de reprendre le contrôle de la ville aux mains des rebelles houthis pro-iraniens. Les forces gouvernementales, soutenues par l'Arabie saoudite, avaient atteint lundi les abords de la ville portuaire de Mocha, les combattants houthistes se retirant dans les terres, selon quatre sources gouvernementales. Le ministre de la Défense a confirmé que la ville située sur la mer Rouge était tombée. Les forces gouvernementales yéménites se sont également emparées de positions clés dans le détroit de Bab el-Mandeb, ont indiqué des sources militaires et gouvernementales, alors que les Houthis ont avancé le mois dernier vers cette voie navigable stratégique. Une grande partie du district de Dhoubab, qui surplombe Bab el-Mandeb, est désormais sous le contrôle de l'armée yéménite, grâce à un soutien aérien massif de la coalition dirigée par l'Arabie saoudite, ont déclaré à Reuters trois sources militaires et une source gouvernementale. Le ministre yéménite de l'Information, Moammar al-Eryani, a précisé à Reuters que l'armée gouvernementale s'était emparée de la piste d'atterrissage de Dhoubab. Située sur le littoral occidental, Dhoubab abrite une base militaire à une trentaine de kilomètres du détroit de Bab el-Mandeb, verrou vers la mer Rouge. Une source militaire gouvernementale affirme toutefois que des combats se poursuivent dans et autour de la base où se trouve la piste d'atterrissage. Les forces soutenues par Ryad ont rapporté que leurs forces navales ont mené une opération militaire dans le gouvernorat d'al Hodeïdah contre les combattants houthistes. Dimanche, le président yéménite, Rachad al Alimi, a annoncé le lancement d'une vaste opération militaire visant à reprendre le contrôle des territoires occupés par les Houthis. Les Houthis contrôlent la capitale depuis 2014, ainsi qu'une grande partie du nord-ouest du pays, où vit la majeure partie de la population. Le mouvement aligné sur l'Iran a déclaré dans la soirée avoir mené trois opérations militaires sur le sol saoudien, visant l'aéroport international du roi Khaled de Ryad, une raffinerie Aramco à Rabigh, l'aéroport international d'Abha ainsi que la base militaire de Khamis Mushait. L'Arabie saoudite n'a pas confirmé dans l'immédiat l'existence de ces attaques. Les médias proches des Houthis avaient auparavant nié toute progression des forces gouvernementales dans la région. Le ministère houthiste de la Santé a fait état de deux morts et sept blessés dans des bombardements de l'armée gouvernementale sur Sanhan et Sa'wan, dans la province de Sanaa. Les combats font rage depuis des semaines sur plusieurs fronts au Yémen, alors que la guerre civile, globalement latente depuis 2022, a regagné en intensité avec le conflit entre les États-Unis et l'Iran. Les Houthis ont notamment entrepris de prendre le contrôle du détroit stratégique de Bab el-Mandeb, et ont lancé plusieurs attaques contre l'Arabie saoudite - alliée des Etats-Unis - et en mer Rouge depuis leur annonce en juillet dernier d'un blocus maritime des ports saoudiens. Alors que les exportations énergétiques du Golfe sont déjà limitées par la fermeture du détroit d'Ormuz par l’Iran, les combats au Yémen menacent cette autre voie énergétique majeure, ce qui a fait grimper les prix mondiaux et fait naître de nouveaux risques. L’Arabie saoudite, qui arme et forme les forces yéménites, soutient la campagne militaire du gouvernement (en exil à Aden)par sa puissance aérienne et a sollicité l’aide logistique de ses alliés pour repousser les Houthis, rétablir la libre circulation en mer Rouge et mettre fin aux attaques sur son territoire. La Turquie et le Pakistan ont discuté avec Ryad du soutien à apporter à leur allié saoudien à l'occasion d'une réunion d'urgence du comité issu du pacte de défense de La Mecque, a annoncé le ministre turc des Affaires étrangères. "Nous avons également discuté de ce qui peut être réalisé pour résoudre le problème pacifiquement à travers le dialogue. L'Arabie saoudite a adopté une approche très constructive pour résoudre le problème", a déclaré Hakan Fidan, à la suite de la réunion. Les trois pays ont par la suite annoncé dans un communiqué commun "le déploiement rapide" de forces militaires en Arabie saoudite. La réunion a permis de "réaffirmer la solidarité et l'unité de nos pays face aux attaques haineuses contre le Royaume et les lieux saints", a réagi le ministère saoudien de la Défense sur X. COMBATS VIOLENTS SE DÉROULENT DANS LE SUD-OUEST DU YÉMEN Les combats les plus violents ces derniers jours ont eu lieu dans le sud-ouest du Yémen, tant dans la zone côtière près du détroit de Bab el-Mandeb qu'autour de la ville de Taïz, dans le sud-ouest, où les Houthis tentent d’encercler les forces gouvernementales. Une agence de presse contrôlée par le groupe rebelle a cité lundi une source militaire affirmant que les Houthis avait chassé les forces gouvernementales du district d’al-Mawasit, dans la province de Taïz, et avait atteint une résidence de Rachad al Alimi. Au cours du week-end, les Houthis ont progressé sur la dernière route reliant Taïz à Aden. La prise de contrôle par les Houthis de la route de Taïz-Aden entraînerait un siège de fait de Taïz, troisième plus grande ville du Yémen, où vivent des centaines de milliers de civils et où sont également stationnés des milliers de soldats des forces gouvernementales. La ville revêt une importance qui ne tient pas uniquement à sa position stratégique : le président yéménite Rachad al Alimi est originaire de cette région et le siège de Taïz exacerberait une situation humanitaire déjà désastreuse dans le pays. La famine au Yémen s'aggrave, avec un nombre record d'habitants incapables de subvenir à leurs besoins alimentaires, a déclaré vendredi le Programme alimentaire mondial (PAM). Le conflit au Yémen a éclaté après la prise de Sanaa par les Houthis en 2014, ce qui a poussé une coalition menée par l’Arabie saoudite à intervenir l’année suivante pour rétablir le gouvernement et chasser le groupe soutenu par l’Iran. Les combats se sont rapidement enlisés dans une impasse sanglante, la plupart des lignes de front étant bloquées. Un cessez-le-feu conclu en 2022 s'est maintenu jusqu’à l'été dernier.

item.title: Dozens quarantined in Siberia after plague institute lab worker dies
item.description: A laboratory worker at a plague research institute in Siberia fell ill and died in undisclosed circumstances, prompting authorities to quarantine dozens of people and the head of Russia's health watchdog to fly to the Irkutsk region.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Osborn
item.content:encoded: A laboratory worker at a plague research institute in Siberia fell ill and died in undisclosed circumstances, prompting authorities to quarantine dozens of people and the head of Russia's health watchdog to fly to the Irkutsk region. The death has sparked public health fears on social media, but the authorities said on Monday the situation was under control. The World Health Organization said that based on available information, "the public health risk to the general population appears to be low". New risk assessments would be conducted once further information became known, it said. US President Donald Trump [USN:L1N45R0V7 TEXT:"said"] the death was a "big problem for Russia" and offered to help Moscow deal with it. "We'll help," Trump said. "Anybody that has that kind of a problem, we're always willing to help." US Secretary of State Marco Rubio [USN:L1N45R0FY TEXT:"said"] Washington was closely monitoring the situation. Plague is endemic to Siberia, location of the first known [USN:L1N42M04M TEXT:"prehistoric human outbreak"], as the bacterium that causes it, Yersinia pestis, is present among the small wild mammals in its vast wilderness and their fleas. It is rare for Russians to fall ill with plague, however, though cases occur every year in other parts of the world — notably Africa. Plague comes in three forms affecting different parts of the body. Pneumonic plague, an infection of the lungs, prompts the patient to cough out infectious airborne droplets. If identified quickly, it can be treated with antibiotics. But if left untreated, it can be fatal in one to six days. Local media have named the laboratory worker who died as Darya Shipilova, a 28-year-old employee at the Irkutsk Anti-Plague Research Institute of Siberia and the Far East. There were conflicting reports about how and where she fell ill, but the authorities said she had died of pneumonia of as-yet unestablished origin. AUTHORITIES SAY NO NEW CASES REPORTED, ALL CONTACTS TRACED Russia's health watchdog, Rospotrebnadzor, told state media the institute had not found evidence of any accidents involving the handling of pathogens after rumours spread on social media that the woman had dropped a test tube containing live bacteria. Nevertheless, Anna Popova, the head of Rospotrebnadzor, flew to Siberia for an emergency meeting over the weekend. According to Russian media reports, about 200 people who had been in contact with the dead woman were quarantined, parts of the hospital in the town of Shelekhov where she died were cordoned off and an aluminium plant told its workers to wear masks. Rospotrebnadzor, in a later statement quoted by the TASS news agency, said officials in Irkutsk Region had found two cases of COVID and two cases of rhinoviruses among people who had been in contact with her. No other cases of infectious diseases were noted. Authorities urged people to remain calm and said there was no evidence that the woman's death was linked to her work. Igor Kobzev, the governor of the Irkutsk region, said in a statement that she had died of "pneumonia of unknown aetiology", adding: "Importantly, over the past few days, no new cases of staff from the Anti-Plague Institute seeking medical attention have been identified." He said the situation was under control and that all known contacts of the dead woman had been identified, examined and placed under medical supervision.

item.title: Italy PM Meloni seeks EU trademark for her voice amid AI deepfake risks
item.description: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni has applied to the European Union Intellectual Property Office (EUIPO) to trademark her voice in a new move to protect herself against AI-generated deepfakes, records showed on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni has applied to the European Union Intellectual Property Office (EUIPO) to trademark her voice in a new move to protect herself against AI-generated deepfakes, records showed on Monday. Her application, dated October 5 on the EUIPO website and confirmed by her office, includes a four-second audio recording of herself twice repeating the phrase, in Italian, "I am Giorgia Meloni." "Io sono Giorgia" ("I am Giorgia") was the title of her 2021 autobiography that echoed a famous declaration Meloni made at a political rally in 2019 and which was even turned into a disco track. Manipulated images of Meloni [USN:L8N41I2DD TEXT:"have repeatedly circulated"] online in recent years and have at times been shared as authentic, including one depicting her sitting on a bed in her underwear. Meloni has denounced such material as part of efforts to spread falsehoods and target individuals, urging users to verify content before sharing it online. She has said that while she is able to defend herself, many others are not. The EUIPO application is still under examination. Italian media have reported that even if approved, it would not by itself prevent the use of her voice in AI-generated deepfakes, though it could create additional legal obstacles for those seeking to replicate it. In 2024, Meloni launched a civil action against a man from Sardinia accused of creating and posting online deepfake pornographic images using her face. The case remains pending before an Italian court.

item.title: Norway boss Solbakken warns of heavy toll on 'thoroughly spent' Haaland
item.description: Norway striker Erling Haaland is showing signs of physical fatigue following a relentless run of matches for club and country, raising concerns over his punishing workload.
item.dc:creator: Tommy Lund
item.content:encoded: Norway striker Erling Haaland is showing signs of physical fatigue following a relentless run of matches for club and country, raising concerns over his punishing workload. The 26-year-old Manchester City forward was substituted after 67 minutes as Norway lost [USN:L6N45Q08D TEXT:"2-1"] away to Portugal in Nations League Group A4 on Sunday. Haaland was among several high-profile players who left the stadium straight after the match on a private jet to make the most of a brief holiday before returning to club duties. "He was simply thoroughly spent," Norway manager Stale Solbakken said of Haaland's condition. "Some of my players have only had six or seven days of holiday. And you do not live off your physical condition in a normal job. Then it is straight into the start of the season, followed by a mini-tournament, so it is an extreme strain." "He’s in the group that carries the heaviest workload — precisely because his team (Manchester City) plays in every tournament and he’s the main man," Solbakken added. Norway midfielder Patrick Berg echoed his manager's assessment, noting the physical toll on Haaland. "He has played all three (Norway) games before this one, so it's not that shocking his strength finally ran out," Berg said. Haaland has endured a gruelling schedule in recent months. Norway's run to the World Cup quarter-finals significantly cut short his off-season and he has since featured in every Premier League match for City, scoring five goals. Haaland highlighted the relentless schedule on social media after a[USN:L6N45H0BY TEXT:" two-goal performance"] in the 3-2 Nations League win over Denmark last month, posting: "So tired. New match in 70 hours." NORWEGIAN PLAYERS' UNION CONCERNED Norwegian players' union NISO expressed concern over the escalating match schedule for the country's leading athletes. "Over time, we have seen a worrying trend where the burden on top players has become far too high," NISO chief Kristoffer Vatshaug said in a press release on Monday. "It has already had consequences for several players. This is serious. "We want clearer guidelines for workload and recovery. It is about the time between matches, consecutive rest periods, travel strain and how much time players get to recover after a long season." Vatshaug said the responsibility does not rest with individual players. "We cannot have a system where protecting players depends on them saying stop themselves. Footballers want to play football. They want to turn out for their club, national team and teammates." Haaland has six days to recover before City resume their Premier League campaign at Liverpool on Sunday.

item.title: TSX ends slightly higher as tech shares rally
item.description: Canada's main stock index ended slightly higher on Monday as investors weighed consolidation in Canada's oil sands sector and the recent selloff in the global bond market, with gains for technology shares offsetting declines for energy and financials.
item.dc:creator: Fergal Smith
item.content:encoded: Canada's main stock index ended slightly higher on Monday as investors weighed consolidation in Canada's oil sands sector and the recent selloff in the global bond market, with gains for technology shares offsetting declines for energy and financials. The Toronto Stock Exchange's S&P/TSX Composite Index (.GSPTSE) ended up 15.9 points, or 0.04%, at 35,518.55, adding to a nearly 1% gain on Friday. "When you've had big moves like you've had in the bond market, that's normally a sign for risk-off in equities, but North American markets keep having a good run," said Greg Taylor, chief investment officer at PenderFund Capital Management. "I think there's still been a lot of cash on the sidelines and people are putting that cash to work and buying any dips and that seems to be what's keeping the market afloat right now," Taylor said. [USN:L1N45R0G4 TEXT:"Borrowing costs"] across major economies remained near multiyear highs as deteriorating public finances, heavy debt issuance and elevated energy prices continue to pressure bond markets. Still, US stocks rose, with the tech-heavy Nasdaq notching a record-high close, as investors focused on a dip in oil prices and looked ahead to quarterly earnings reports. The TSX's technology sector (.SPTTTK) advanced 1.4%, with shares of e-commerce company Shopify (SHOP.TO) adding 5.7%. Cenovus Energy (CVE.TO) said it would buy Athabasca Oil (ATH.TO) in a C$5.7 billion ($4 billion) cash-and-stock deal, cementing its position as one of Canada's largest oil sands producers at a time the country is aiming to boost crude output. Cenovus lost 3%, while Athabasca was up 13.5%. [USN:L6N45R01S TEXT:"Suncor Energy"] (SU.TO) ended 1.2% lower after the company agreed to sell its interests in three offshore oil assets to London-based Ithaca Energy (ITH.L) for C$1.2 billion ($841.69 million) in upfront cash. [USN:L1N45Q068 TEXT:"US crude oil futures"] settled down 1.8% at $89.43 a barrel after crude exports from the Middle East increased and the Group of Seven nations pledged to boost supplies. Energy (.SPTTEN) fell 0.4% and heavily weighted financials (.SPTTFS) were down 0.5%.

item.title: Nasdaq notches record high close as investors focus on earnings
item.description: The Nasdaq notched a record high close on Monday, lifted by Nvidia and Microsoft, as investors focused on a dip in oil prices and looked ahead to quarterly earnings reports.
item.dc:creator: Noel Randewich
item.content:encoded: The Nasdaq notched a record high close on Monday, lifted by Nvidia and Microsoft, as investors focused on a dip in oil prices and looked ahead to quarterly earnings reports. It was the Nasdaq's second day of sharp gains after weaker-than-expected jobs data on Friday dampened expectations for an interest rate hike from the Federal Reserve at its policy meeting this month. The S&P 500 rose and was about 0.3% below its August 13 record high close. AI heavyweight Nvidia (NVDA.O) climbed 2.1% and also reached a record-high close, boosting its stock market value to $5.76 trillion. Microsoft (MSFT.O) added 1.5%, while Meta Platforms (META.O) and Tesla (TSLA.O) gained about 2% each. Oil prices slipped after crude exports from the Middle East increased and the Group of Seven nations pledged to boost supplies. "With the economic data calendar being light and earnings about a week away, investors are really groping for anything positive to glom onto, and clearly they're looking at lower energy prices," said Art Hogan, chief market strategist at B. Riley Wealth. BANKS KICK OFF THIRD-QUARTER RESULTS Third-quarter earnings season kicks off next week with reports from large US banks. Analysts on average see S&P 500 earnings jumping over 30% year over year, thanks largely to AI-related stocks, according to LSEG data. Following jobs data on Friday that showed US job growth slowed more than expected in September, traders see a 24% chance of an interest rate hike at the Fed's October meeting, down from a 70% chance a week ago, according to CME's FedWatch tool. PTC (PTC.O) surged 33% after France's Schneider Electric (SCHN.PA) agreed to [USN:L6N45Q07P TEXT:"acquire"] the software firm in a $22.6 billion all-cash deal. The S&P 500 climbed 0.66% to end the session at 7,773.95 points. The Nasdaq gained 1.05% to 27,477.31 points, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.18% to 51,267.90 points. The Nasdaq's previous record high close was on September 22. Ten of the 11 S&P 500 sector indexes rose, led by materials (.SPLRCM) , up 1.22%, followed by a 1.14% gain in communication services (.SPLRCL) . Optimism about robust corporate earnings has helped US stocks outperform global rivals in the last six months, despite rising Treasury yields and higher oil prices related to the US war with Iran. RXO (RXO.N) jumped over 22% after logistics firm C.H. Robinson Worldwide (CHRW.O) agreed [USN:L4N45R0MP TEXT:"to buy"] the transportation broker in a stock-and-cash transaction for $5.8 billion. C.H. Robinson (CHRW.O) fell nearly 11%. [USN:L4N45O1CT TEXT:"Cerebras Systems"] (CBRS.O) rose 9% after OpenAI CEO Sam Altman said on social media the chip designer is a "close partner" and that the companies have "deep engagement pushing on the frontiers of speed." Advancing issues outnumbered falling ones within the S&P 500 (.AD.SPX) by a 1.7-to-1 ratio. The S&P 500 posted 13 new highs and 20 new lows; the Nasdaq recorded 57 new highs and 243 new lows. Volume on US exchanges was relatively light, with 16.8 billion shares traded, compared to an average of 17.3 billion shares over the previous 20 sessions.

item.title: Brazil markets' Bolsonaro rally sends stock exchange to record high
item.description: Brazil's main stock exchange surged to a record high on Monday as the country's markets cheered on right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro's better-than-expected finish in the first round of Sunday's presidential election.
item.dc:creator: Oliver Griffin, Marcela Ayres, Gabriel Araujo
item.content:encoded: Brazil's main stock exchange surged to a record high on Monday as the country's markets cheered on right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro's better-than-expected finish in the first round of Sunday's presidential election. Brazil's Bovespa index (.BVSP) settled at 206,911.89 points, a new closing record, after a 7.7% jump, the largest since March 24, 2020. The eldest son of former right-wing President Jair Bolsonaro won 47% of the votes cast on Sunday and will face leftist incumbent President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, who secured about 45% of the vote, in a runoff on October 25. Polls had forecast Lula would lead the first round of voting by around three percentage points. Investors cheered on Monday as Bolsonaro's strong showing was matched by [USN:L1N45L166 TEXT:"gains for his allies in Congress"]. Analysts say a friendlier legislature would make it easier for him, if elected, to push through a pro-business agenda of tighter public spending, privatizations and tax cuts. In Washington, President Donald Trump joined the celebration, [USN:L6N45R139 TEXT:"calling his first-place finish"] a "very, very big victory" and predicting a close runoff. "Brazil wants change," Bolsonaro said on Sunday evening, heralding the "end of the era of (Lula's) Workers' Party." [USN:L1N45R0KI TEXT:"Reuters exclusively reported"] on Monday that Lula is considering tapping Vice President Geraldo Alckmin to be his next finance minister if re-elected, in a bid to bolster the government's fiscal credibility and win over centrist voters in the wake of Bolsonaro's first-round success. Retailer Magazine Luiza (MGLU3.SA) , conglomerate Cosan (CSAN3.SA) and stock exchange operator B3 (B3SA3.SA) were among the main gainers, with each jumping more than 20%, while oil company Petrobras rose just over 8% and lender Bradesco was up over 13%. The benchmark index had its best daily performance since March 2020, when markets faced extreme volatility at the start of the COVID-19 pandemic. US-traded shares of Brazilian companies also soared, with brokerage XP (XP.O) up 33%, digital lender Nu Holdings (NU.N) up 13%, and fintech firms StoneCo (STNE.O) and PagBank (PAGS.N) each up more than 20%. The cost of buying insurance on Brazilian government debt through credit default swaps fell 20 basis points as traders bet on an improvement in the country's finances. J.P. Morgan upgraded Brazil's equities to "overweight" on Monday, saying a more favorable political backdrop after recent election developments had improved the outlook for the region's largest market and could drive a period of outperformance. Sunday's vote sent the country's currency strengthening 4.1% to around 5 per dollar, putting it on track for its biggest one-day gain in four years since the elder Bolsonaro [USN:L1N3130Q9 TEXT:"performed better than expected"] against Lula in the first round of the 2022 election. He went on to lose to Lula in the second round of that election and was subsequently convicted of trying to carry out a coup to overturn the result. The former president was sentenced to about 27 years in prison and is currently under house arrest. Brazil's international debt also rallied on Monday, while broader fixed-income markets were jittery. The 2056 bond was up 1.4 cents on the dollar to bid at 93.5 cents, Tradeweb data showed. 'THE MARKET WANTS CHANGE' Bolsonaro has pitched himself as a "more centered" version of his father to investors concerned about Brazil's burgeoning fiscal pressures. "It remains to be seen whether the senator would ultimately prove more fiscally responsible than Lula would be in a fourth non-consecutive presidential term. However, markets are likely to give him the benefit of the doubt," said Thierry Larose, portfolio manager at Vontobel. If he is elected, Bolsonaro would enjoy some room to maneuver with Congress after his Liberal Party emerged as the [USN:L1N45L166 TEXT:"biggest winner"] in congressional races on Sunday. His Liberal Party (PL) increased its representation in the Senate from 15 to 28 seats, the strongest result for a party since Brazil's constitution was enacted in the late 1980s, following the country's return to democracy. It also is projected to secure 121 seats in the 513-seat lower house, up from its current 98 seats. "The likelihood of advancing reforms is much greater," said Pedro Paulo Silveira, an analyst at Terra Investimentos. He noted that during the previous Bolsonaro government, reforms often depended on costly political bargaining or stalled altogether. Analysts also expect the real to continue strengthening into 2027. Societe Generale forecast that it would move to 5.10 by the end of 2026, with scope to move below 5.00 in the first half of 2027. Morgan Stanley forecast the real could strengthen past 4.90 and toward 4.50 in the first quarter of next year. "The market wants change, it wants reform, it doesn't want a high public deficit; with the current government, all of this will continue," said Pedro Galdi, investment analyst at the AGF Investments platform. Bolsonaro's strong showing is likely to boost market confidence in the near term, said Bryan Harris, a managing partner at Sabio. "The market will be looking for clear signals from Bolsonaro that he is serious about tackling the country's problems," Harris said. Heading into Sunday's vote, most private polls, which largely underestimated the younger Bolsonaro's strength, had shown the 45-year-old senator and Lula, who will turn 81 later this month, about even in a runoff vote.

item.title: Trump's deportation push forces dozens of LGBT migrants onto hostile terrain
item.description: Two years ago, a mob assaulted Abdou Latifou and threatened to kill him after he was seen kissing the man he loved.
item.dc:creator: Robbie Corey-Boulet, Kristina Cooke, Ngouda Dione, Loucoumane Coulibaly
item.content:encoded: Two years ago, a mob assaulted Abdou Latifou and threatened to kill him after he was seen kissing the man he loved. He fled his home in the West African nation of Togo and sought refuge in the United States, according to his asylum application. Latifou rejoiced last November when a US immigration judge ruled it was not safe for him to be sent home. “I told myself, ‘From this day on, I’m entering a world where I’m free to live as myself,’” he said. In June, though, Latifou was forced onto a US deportation plane — not back to Togo but to Sierra Leone, a nation where gay men can be sentenced to life in prison under colonial-era laws. President Donald Trump's administration has [USN:L6N45K0X3 TEXT:"deported"] tens of thousands of people to third countries, enabled by [USN:L6N41T01V TEXT:"deals"] with impoverished foreign governments. Latifou's case is one of 40 documented by Reuters where migrants granted US legal protection after being persecuted for their LGBT status were deported to third countries in Africa that either criminalize same-sex relations or have been described by the State Department as [USN:L6N42P15Q TEXT:"hostile to LGBT people"]. Reuters has tracked the fate of all 40 – including people from across Africa, as well as Iraq, Jamaica and Russia – by interviewing a dozen deportees and immigration lawyers and reviewing hundreds of pages of legal documents. Sixteen remain in the countries they were deported to and some are [USN:L6N44Z0DP TEXT:"still detained"]. Sixteen others, like Latifou, were repatriated to their home countries against their will. Nine are in hiding in third locations. One Ghanaian man is no longer in contact with his lawyers or relatives, they said. Sending people “to a third country where they face the very persecution we recognized makes a mockery of our protection systems,” said Claire Trickler-McNulty, a former senior US immigration official. Immigration and Customs Enforcement "does not enforce the law on the basis of sexual orientation, that would be illegal,” Chandler Rebel, a spokesman for the Department of Homeland Security, ICE's parent agency, said in a statement. "Third country removals are an essential public safety tool.” A NEW TACTIC Third-country deportations were rare before Trump’s second term. But since he returned to office and began a wide-ranging immigration crackdown, more than 40,000 people in total have been deported to countries not their own by ICE and Border Patrol, according to preliminary government data shared with Reuters, far higher than previous estimates from advocates. About 900 were sent to African countries. In a February order, in a case challenging the policy, US District Judge Brian Murphy highlighted the risks facing gay people. The government’s claim that those targeted had not explicitly asked not to be deported to repressive third countries was an “absurdity,” he wrote. “No person could reasonably be expected to make detailed, prophylactic claims about every country on Earth to which she might have a valid claim against removal.” On Tuesday, the Supreme Court [USN:S0N43100Z TEXT:"put a hold on Murphy's ruling"], allowing the administration to continue third-country deportations. The court will hear arguments in December. HOSTILE GROUND The 40 cases documented by Reuters involve deportations to three countries that explicitly criminalize same-sex sexual acts: Sierra Leone, Cameroon and Eswatini. In three other countries that do not have such laws on the books -- Central African Republic, Equatorial Guinea and the Democratic Republic of Congo -- the State Department has previously documented abuses against LGBT people, including “corrective rape” and conversion therapy. Government spokespeople for the six countries did not respond to requests for comment. Bridget Crawford, director of law and policy at Immigration Equality, an LGBT advocacy group, said the US has repeatedly granted asylum to LGBT people from these countries. Her group has helped 12 Cameroonians and one person from Congo win asylum in recent years. But more than half of the 40, including Latifou, were not eligible for asylum because they did not apply for it in countries they passed through before illegally entering the US. This was disqualifying under [USN:L6N3M70NW TEXT:"Biden-era restrictions"] that a federal court vacated in May. The judge in Latifou's case granted a lesser protection, barring the government from deporting him to Togo but allowing his removal elsewhere.
